attributes.description: Reference to the Water Treatment Plant (WTP) or Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) facility where the membrane system is installed. Links to the facility master.

attributes.name: secondary_membrane_registry_id
attributes.description: Reference to the membrane module or rack asset record in IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS). Enables lifecycle tracking and maintenance history linkage.
attributes.references: ISO 55001 Asset Management; IBM Maximo Asset Management

attributes.name: secondary_membrane_wtp_facility_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Water Treatment Plant (WTP) or Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) facility where the membrane system is installed. Links to the facility master.

attributes.name: mor_submission_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treatment.mor_submission. Business justification: Membrane performance records are reported in Monthly Operating Reports (MOR) when mor_reportable flag is true. This FK links membrane performance metrics to the MOR submission for regulatory reporting

attributes.name: pressure_zone_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.pressure_zone. Business justification: Membrane treatment units serve specific pressure zones. Performance monitoring (flux decline, TMP increase, recovery rate) is tracked in context of zone demand and water quality requirements. Essentia

attributes.name: scada_tag_id
attributes.description: Reference to the OSIsoft PI Historian tag that is the source of real-time SCADA process data for this membrane performance record.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; SCADA Integration Standards

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the IBM Maximo work order associated with a chemical cleaning event or integrity test that generated this performance record.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; AWWA M53

attributes.name: backwash_frequency_per_day
attributes.description: Number of backwash cycles performed per day on the membrane unit. Applicable to UF and MF systems. Increasing frequency indicates fouling progression and may trigger a chemical cleaning event.

attributes.name: chemical_cleaning_count
attributes.description: Cumulative number of chemical cleaning events (Clean-In-Place / CIP) performed on this membrane unit since installation. Excessive cleaning frequency indicates accelerated fouling and may signal replacement need.

attributes.name: cleaning_chemical_type
attributes.description: Type of chemical agent used in the most recent Clean-In-Place (CIP) cleaning event (e.g., citric acid, sodium hydroxide, sodium hypochlorite, EDTA, enzyme cleaner). Relevant for chemical compatibility and O&M cost tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: citric_acid|sodium_hydroxide|sodium_hypochlorite|EDTA|enzyme|sulfuric_acid|hydrochloric_acid — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AWWA M53; manufacturer CIP guidelines; SAP MM

attributes.name: concentrate_pressure_psi
attributes.description: Pressure of the concentrate (reject) stream exiting the membrane system in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI). Used in net driving pressure calculations and energy recovery assessments.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this membrane performance record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Audit trail field for data lineage and regulatory traceability.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; GASB; EPA data retention requirements

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Origin system or method by which this performance record was captured: pi_historian (OSIsoft PI Historian automated), scada_manual (SCADA operator entry), lims (LIMS laboratory result), cmms_manual (IBM Maximo manual entry), or calculated (derived value).
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; IBM Maximo; LIMS LabWare; SCADA

attributes.name: feed_flow_rate_gpm
attributes.description: Volumetric flow rate of feed water entering the membrane system in Gallons Per Minute (GPM). Sourced from OSIsoft PI Historian SCADA data.

attributes.name: feed_pressure_psi
attributes.description: Inlet feed water pressure to the membrane system in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI). Used to calculate net driving pressure and assess pump performance.

attributes.name: feed_tds_mg_l
attributes.description: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) concentration of the feed water in milligrams per litre (mg/L). Used to calculate salt rejection rate for RO systems and assess scaling potential.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; Standard Methods 2540C; EPA SDWA

attributes.name: feed_temperature_c
attributes.description: Temperature of the feed water in degrees Celsius at the membrane inlet. Used for temperature correction of normalized flux calculations per ASTM D6908. Lower temperatures increase viscosity and reduce flux.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; ASTM D6908; SCADA/OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: feed_turbidity_ntu
attributes.description: Turbidity of the feed water entering the membrane system measured in Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU). Elevated feed turbidity increases fouling rate and cleaning frequency.
attributes.references: EPA LT2ESWTR; AWWA M53; Standard Methods 2130

attributes.name: flux_decline_pct
attributes.description: Percentage decline in normalized permeate flux from the baseline (clean membrane) value, calculated as (baseline flux - current flux) / baseline flux × 100. Triggers chemical cleaning when threshold is exceeded per O&M protocol.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; ASTM D6908; manufacturer O&M guidelines

attributes.name: fouling_index
attributes.description: Silt Density Index (SDI) or Modified Fouling Index (MFI) of the feed water, indicating the fouling potential. Higher values indicate greater particulate loading and predict more frequent cleaning cycles. Applicable primarily to RO systems.

attributes.name: installation_date
attributes.description: Date the membrane element or module was installed in service at the treatment facility. Used to calculate membrane age and remaining useful life for replacement planning.

attributes.name: integrity_test_date
attributes.description: Date on which the most recent Direct Integrity Test (DIT) was performed on the membrane unit. Required at minimum daily under EPA LT2ESWTR for membrane systems claiming Cryptosporidium log removal credit.
attributes.references: EPA LT2ESWTR; 40 CFR Part 141.719; AWWA M53

attributes.name: integrity_test_result
attributes.description: Outcome of the Direct Integrity Test (DIT) or pressure decay test for the membrane unit: pass, fail, or inconclusive. A fail result triggers regulatory notification and corrective action under EPA LT2ESWTR.
attributes.references: EPA LT2ESWTR; 40 CFR Part 141.719; AWWA M53

attributes.name: last_chemical_cleaning_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent chemical cleaning event (Clean-In-Place / CIP) performed on the membrane unit. Used to track cleaning frequency and correlate with performance recovery.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; IBM Maximo CMMS Work Order History

attributes.name: log_removal_value
attributes.description: Calculated Log Removal Value (LRV) for Cryptosporidium or other target pathogens based on the integrity test results. Must meet or exceed the treatment credit assigned by the state primacy agency under EPA LT2ESWTR.
attributes.references: EPA LT2ESWTR; 40 CFR Part 141.719; State Primacy Agency

attributes.name: membrane_age_days
attributes.description: Number of days the membrane has been in service since installation date. Used for lifecycle management, replacement planning, and performance degradation trending.

attributes.name: membrane_configuration
attributes.description: Physical configuration of the membrane element: spiral wound (common for RO/NF), hollow fiber (common for UF/MF), tubular, or flat sheet. Affects cleaning protocols and flux benchmarks.

attributes.name: membrane_technology_type
attributes.description: Classification of the membrane filtration technology: Reverse Osmosis (RO), Ultrafiltration (UF), Microfiltration (MF), Nanofiltration (NF), or Electrodialysis Reversal (EDR). Drives applicable performance benchmarks and regulatory thresholds.
attributes.references: AWWA M53 Membrane Filtration; EPA LT2ESWTR; ISO 4650

attributes.name: membrane_unit_tag
attributes.description: Plant-level equipment tag identifier for the specific membrane module, rack, or train (e.g., MEM-RO-01, UF-RACK-03). Aligns with P&ID and SCADA/HMI tag naming conventions.

attributes.name: mor_reportable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this performance record contains data that must be included in the Monthly Operating Report (MOR) submitted to the state primacy agency. Supports regulatory compliance workflow.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency MOR requirements; 40 CFR Part 141

attributes.name: normalized_permeate_flux
attributes.description: Temperature-corrected normalized permeate flux in litres per square metre per hour (L/m²/h). The principal performance indicator for membrane productivity; decline over time indicates fouling or scaling. Normalized to 25°C per ASTM D6908.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; ASTM D6908; EPA LT2ESWTR

attributes.name: observation_timestamp
attributes.description: The principal real-world timestamp when the membrane performance measurement or test was recorded, sourced from OSIsoft PI Historian or SCADA system. Distinct from record audit timestamps.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; EPA MOR; AWWA M53

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the membrane unit: online (in production), offline (out of service), cleaning (undergoing chemical cleaning), integrity_test (under pressure decay test), standby, or decommissioned. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: online|offline|cleaning|integrity_test|standby|decommissioned — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AWWA M53; SCADA/HMI operational standards; ISO 55001

attributes.name: permeate_flow_rate_gpm
attributes.description: Volumetric flow rate of product water (permeate) exiting the membrane system in Gallons Per Minute (GPM). Used to calculate system recovery and normalized flux.

attributes.name: permeate_pressure_psi
attributes.description: Pressure on the permeate (product water) side of the membrane in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI). Used in TMP calculation and system hydraulic analysis.

attributes.name: permeate_tds_mg_l
attributes.description: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS) concentration of the permeate (product water) in milligrams per litre (mg/L). Used to calculate salt rejection rate and verify finished water quality compliance.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; Standard Methods 2540C; EPA SDWA MCL

attributes.name: permeate_turbidity_ntu
attributes.description: Turbidity of the permeate (filtered product water) exiting the membrane system in Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU). Must meet MCL of 0.3 NTU (95th percentile) under EPA Surface Water Treatment Rule.
attributes.references: EPA SWTR; 40 CFR Part 141.173; AWWA M53

attributes.name: pressure_decay_rate
attributes.description: Rate of pressure decay (psi/min or kPa/min) measured during a Direct Integrity Test (DIT) / pressure decay test. Exceeding the control limit indicates a breach in membrane integrity requiring investigation per EPA LT2ESWTR.
attributes.references: EPA LT2ESWTR; AWWA M53; 40 CFR Part 141.719

attributes.name: record_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this performance record, formatted as MEM-{UNIT_CODE}-{YYYYMMDD}-{SEQUENCE}. Used in Monthly Operating Reports (MOR) and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: EPA MOR Reporting; AWWA M53 Membrane Filtration

attributes.name: recovery_rate_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of feed water converted to permeate (product water), calculated as (permeate flow / feed flow) × 100. Higher recovery reduces waste but increases scaling risk. Key operational efficiency metric.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; EPA Water Efficiency Guidelines

attributes.name: replacement_recommended
attributes.description: Flag indicating whether the membrane unit has been assessed as requiring replacement based on performance degradation, age, or failed integrity tests. Drives capital planning and procurement activities.
attributes.references: ISO 55001 Asset Management; AWWA M53; CIP planning

attributes.name: salt_rejection_rate_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of dissolved salts (Total Dissolved Solids / TDS) rejected by the RO or NF membrane, calculated as (1 - permeate TDS / feed TDS) × 100. Applicable to RO and NF systems only. Decline indicates membrane integrity loss.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; ASTM D6908; EPA SDWA

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer-assigned serial number for the individual membrane element or module. Enables traceability for warranty claims and failure analysis.
attributes.references: ISO 55001; AWWA M53; IBM Maximo Asset Management

attributes.name: specific_energy_consumption_kwh_m3
attributes.description: Energy consumed per cubic metre of permeate produced (kWh/m³). Key operational efficiency and OPEX metric for membrane systems, particularly RO. Increasing values indicate pump inefficiency or fouling.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; EPA WaterSense; EPRI Water & Wastewater Energy Benchmarking

attributes.name: tmp_increase_pct
attributes.description: Percentage increase in Transmembrane Pressure (TMP) from the baseline (clean membrane) value. A TMP increase exceeding the O&M threshold (typically 15-20%) triggers a chemical cleaning event.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; ASTM D6908; manufacturer O&M guidelines

attributes.name: transmembrane_pressure_psi
attributes.description: Transmembrane Pressure (TMP) measured in Pounds per Square Inch (PSI), representing the pressure differential across the membrane. Rising TMP at constant flux indicates fouling. Key SCADA-sourced process control parameter.
attributes.references: AWWA M53; ASTM D6908; SCADA/OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: turbidity_removal_efficiency_pct
attributes.description: Percentage reduction in turbidity (NTU) across the membrane system, calculated as (1 - permeate NTU / feed NTU) × 100. Applicable to UF and MF systems. Regulatory compliance metric under EPA LT2ESWTR.
attributes.references: EPA LT2ESWTR; AWWA M53; 40 CFR Part 141

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this membrane performance record was last modified in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Supports data quality auditing and change tracking.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; GASB; EPA data retention requirements

attributes.name: secondary_uv_wtp_facility_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Water Treatment Plant or Wastewater Treatment Plant where this UV disinfection event occurred. Supports facility-level regulatory reporting and MOR submissions.
attributes.references: EPA Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA); State Drinking Water Primacy Agencies

attributes.name: acknowledgment_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the certified operator acknowledged this UV disinfection event record. Null if not yet acknowledged. Provides audit trail for regulatory compliance and response time tracking.
attributes.references: State Drinking Water Primacy Agencies; EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); SDWA

attributes.name: corrective_action_taken
attributes.description: Free-text description of the corrective action taken by the operator in response to a non-compliant or alarm UV disinfection event (e.g., lamp replacement, sleeve cleaning, flow reduction, system bypass). Null for compliant operational events. Required for regulatory non-compliance documentation.
attributes.references: EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); State Drinking Water Primacy Agencies; SDWA

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this UV disinfection event record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Represents the audit trail creation timestamp, distinct from the event_timestamp which captures the real-world measurement time.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; GASB data governance standards; Databricks Lakehouse audit requirements

attributes.name: data_quality_flag
attributes.description: Quality indicator for this UV disinfection event record as assessed during ETL ingestion from OSIsoft PI Historian: good (validated measurement), suspect (possible sensor anomaly), bad (confirmed sensor failure or out-of-range), missing (gap-filled), or interpolated (value estimated between readings). Used for data quality governance and exclusion from regulatory calculations.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian data quality standards; AWWA M75; EPA data quality requirements for regulatory reporting

attributes.name: dose_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether the delivered UV dose (uv_dose_delivered_mj_cm2) met or exceeded the required UV dose (uv_dose_required_mj_cm2) for regulatory log inactivation credit. True = compliant; False = non-compliant. Core field for regulatory reporting and MOR submissions.
attributes.references: EPA LT2ESWTR (40 CFR Part 141); EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); State Drinking Water Primacy Agencies

attributes.name: event_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of this UV disinfection event record: compliant (dose requirements met), non_compliant (dose requirements not met), pending_review (awaiting operator or QA review), or voided (record invalidated). Drives regulatory compliance workflow and MOR submission readiness.
attributes.references: EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); State Drinking Water Primacy Agencies; SDWA

attributes.name: event_timestamp
attributes.description: The precise date and time (ISO 8601 with timezone offset) at which the UV disinfection event observation or measurement was recorded by the SCADA/PI Historian system. This is the principal real-world event time used for regulatory log inactivation credit verification and MOR reporting.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); AWWA M75

attributes.name: event_type
attributes.description: Classification of the UV disinfection event: operational (normal periodic reading), alarm (threshold breach), fault (equipment failure), startup (reactor coming online), shutdown (reactor going offline), or maintenance (scheduled service window). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: operational|alarm|fault|startup|shutdown|maintenance — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
attributes.references: AWWA M75 - UV Disinfection; EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006)

attributes.name: flow_rate_gpm
attributes.business_glossary_term: Flow Rate Through Reactor (GPM - Gallons Per Minute)
attributes.description: Volumetric flow rate of water passing through the UV reactor at the time of the event, measured in gallons per minute (GPM). Sourced from the flow meter via SCADA/PI Historian. A key variable in UV dose calculation; higher flow rates reduce hydraulic retention time and effective dose.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; AWWA M75; EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006)

tag_set.value: Flow Rate Through Reactor (GPM - Gallons Per Minute)

attributes.name: flow_rate_mgd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Flow Rate Through Reactor (MGD - Million Gallons per Day)
attributes.description: Volumetric flow rate of water passing through the UV reactor expressed in million gallons per day (MGD). Derived from the GPM reading for facility-level production reporting, MOR submissions, and capacity utilization analytics.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; AWWA M75; EPA Monthly Operating Report (MOR) requirements

tag_set.value: Flow Rate Through Reactor (MGD - Million Gallons per Day)

attributes.name: lamp_hours_elapsed
attributes.description: Cumulative operating hours logged on the UV lamp(s) at the time of this event. Used to track lamp aging, predict end-of-life, and schedule preventive lamp replacement per manufacturer recommendations and CMMS work orders.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS); AWWA M75; UV lamp manufacturer specifications

attributes.name: lamp_power_pct
attributes.description: Current power output of the UV lamp(s) expressed as a percentage of rated maximum power (0–100%). Controlled by the Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) or ballast controller. Used to assess lamp performance degradation and energy efficiency.
attributes.references: AWWA M75; EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); VFD/ballast manufacturer specifications

attributes.name: lamp_rated_hours
attributes.description: Manufacturer-rated maximum operating hours for the UV lamp before replacement is required. Used in conjunction with lamp_hours_elapsed to calculate remaining lamp life and trigger preventive maintenance work orders in IBM Maximo.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS); UV lamp manufacturer specifications; AWWA M75

attributes.name: lamp_status
attributes.description: Operational status of the UV lamp(s) in the reactor at the time of the event: on (operating normally), off (intentionally de-energized), fault (lamp failure or electrical fault detected), warming_up (lamp in pre-operational warm-up phase), or end_of_life (lamp hours exceeded rated life). Sourced from SCADA/PLC lamp monitoring.
attributes.references: AWWA M75; EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: log_inactivation_target
attributes.description: The required log inactivation credit (e.g., 2.0-log, 3.0-log, 4.0-log) for the target pathogen as mandated by the applicable regulatory treatment technique (e.g., LT2ESWTR Cryptosporidium bin assignment). Expressed as a decimal log value. Determines the required UV dose threshold.
attributes.references: EPA LT2ESWTR (40 CFR Part 141); EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); State Drinking Water Primacy Agencies

attributes.name: mor_included_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether this UV disinfection event record has been included in the Monthly Operating Report (MOR) submission for the applicable reporting period. True = included in MOR; False = excluded (e.g., voided, data quality issue). Supports MOR completeness verification.
attributes.references: EPA Monthly Operating Report (MOR) requirements; State Drinking Water Primacy Agencies; SDWA

attributes.name: operator_acknowledged_flag
attributes.description: Boolean indicator of whether a certified operator has reviewed and acknowledged this UV disinfection event record, particularly for non-compliant or alarm events. True = acknowledged; False = pending acknowledgment. Required for regulatory audit trails and MOR documentation.
attributes.references: State Drinking Water Primacy Agencies; EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); SDWA operator certification requirements

attributes.name: pi_historian_tag
attributes.description: The OSIsoft PI Historian tag name or point name associated with this UV reactor event record (e.g., 'WTP1.UV.BANK1.DOSE'). Enables direct traceability from the Silver Layer record back to the source PI Historian time-series data point for data lineage and quality validation.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; SCADA data integration standards

attributes.name: reactor_bank_number
attributes.description: Sequential number identifying the UV reactor bank or train within the treatment facility (e.g., Bank 1, Bank 2). Multiple reactor banks may operate in series or parallel. Used for bank-level performance comparison and redundancy management.
attributes.references: AWWA M75; EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006)

attributes.name: sensor_reading_mv
attributes.description: Raw millivolt (mV) output from the UV intensity sensor (radiometer) within the reactor, as recorded by the SCADA/PI Historian system before conversion to mW/cm². Retained for sensor calibration verification and data quality auditing.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; AWWA M75; UV reactor manufacturer calibration procedures

attributes.name: sleeve_fouling_factor
attributes.description: Dimensionless correction factor (0.0–1.0) representing the degree of fouling on the UV lamp quartz sleeve. A value of 1.0 indicates a clean sleeve; lower values indicate fouling that reduces UV transmittance through the sleeve and effective dose delivery. Used in dose calculation models and sleeve cleaning scheduling.
attributes.references: EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); AWWA M75; UV reactor manufacturer validation reports

attributes.name: target_pathogen
attributes.description: The primary pathogen for which the UV dose and log inactivation credit is being calculated and verified: Cryptosporidium, Giardia, virus, or bacteria. Determines the applicable dose-response curve and regulatory credit table used in compliance assessment.
attributes.references: EPA LT2ESWTR (40 CFR Part 141); EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); AWWA M75

attributes.name: turbidity_ntu
attributes.description: Turbidity of the water entering the UV reactor, measured in Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU). High turbidity can shield pathogens from UV exposure and reduce disinfection efficacy. Sourced from inline turbidimeter via SCADA/PI Historian.
attributes.references: EPA Surface Water Treatment Rule (40 CFR Part 141); AWWA M75; Standard Methods 2130

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this UV disinfection event record was last modified in the Silver Layer lakehouse (e.g., operator acknowledgment, corrective action update, data quality flag revision). Supports audit trail and change tracking requirements.
attributes.references: ISO 9001 Quality Management; GASB data governance standards; Databricks Lakehouse audit requirements

attributes.name: uv_dose_delivered_mj_cm2
attributes.description: Calculated UV dose actually delivered to the water stream, expressed in millijoules per square centimeter (mJ/cm²). Computed by the UV reactor control system using validated dose-response models incorporating UV intensity, UVT, and flow rate. This is the primary metric for log inactivation credit verification.
attributes.references: EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); AWWA M75; 40 CFR Part 141 (LT2ESWTR)

attributes.name: uv_dose_required_mj_cm2
attributes.description: Minimum UV dose required to achieve the regulatory log inactivation credit for the target pathogen (e.g., Cryptosporidium, Giardia, viruses), expressed in mJ/cm². Defined by the applicable regulatory treatment technique requirement (e.g., LT2ESWTR). Used to determine dose compliance status.
attributes.references: EPA LT2ESWTR (40 CFR Part 141); EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); AWWA M75

attributes.name: uv_intensity_mw_cm2
attributes.description: Measured UV irradiance at the sensor within the reactor, expressed in milliwatts per square centimeter (mW/cm²). Sourced from the UV sensor array via SCADA/PI Historian. Critical input for UV dose calculation and lamp performance monitoring.
attributes.references: EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); AWWA M75; NSF/ANSI 55

attributes.name: uv_transmittance_pct
attributes.description: Ultraviolet transmittance of the water at 254 nm, expressed as a percentage (UVT%). Measured by an online UVT analyzer or photometer. Directly affects the effective UV dose delivered to pathogens; lower UVT reduces dose efficiency.
attributes.references: EPA UV Disinfection Guidance Manual (2006); AWWA M75; Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: water_temperature_c
attributes.description: Temperature of the water passing through the UV reactor at the time of the event, measured in degrees Celsius. Water temperature affects UV transmittance and lamp output efficiency. Sourced from inline temperature sensor via SCADA/PI Historian.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; AWWA M75; Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

products.name: sludge_production
products.description: Tracks sludge and residuals generation from water and wastewater treatment processes. Captures sludge type (alum sludge, lime sludge, biological sludge, filter backwash solids), volume generated (gallons/dry tons), solids concentration (% TS), dewatering method (centrifuge, belt press, drying beds), cake solids content, disposal method (landfill, land application, incineration), and disposal manifest reference. Supports residuals management compliance and NPDES permit reporting.
products.reference: Residuals / Biosolids Production Record

attributes.name: sludge_production_id
attributes.description: Unique surrogate identifier for each sludge production record in the treatment domain. Primary key for the sludge_production data product.

attributes.name: commissioning_activity_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.commissioning_activity. Business justification: Sludge handling system testing during commissioning validates dewatering equipment and disposal processes. Operational turnover requires demonstration of residuals handling per design specifications.

attributes.name: dma_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to distribution.dma. Business justification: Sludge disposal and biosolids hauling routes are planned by DMA for logistics optimization and cost allocation. Some utilities track treatment residuals generation in context of service area for full-

attributes.name: facility_id
attributes.description: Reference to the Water Treatment Plant (WTP) or Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) where the sludge was generated. Links to the facility master record.
attributes.references: AWWA M36 Water Audits and Loss Control Programs; EPA NPDES Permit Program

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Sludge disposal has significant cost (disposal_cost_usd field present). Required for waste disposal expense tracking, environmental compliance cost reporting, budget monitoring, and GL posting of disp

attributes.name: hauler_vendor_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to supply.vendor. Business justification: Biosolids hauling and disposal contractors are vendors providing services under contracts with performance requirements, insurance, and regulatory compliance. Essential for vendor performance tracking

attributes.name: lab_sample_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Sample ID
attributes.description: Reference identifier for the associated analytical sample record in the LIMS (LabWare or equivalent). Links sludge production records to laboratory test results for total solids, volatile solids, metals, pathogens, and other quality parameters.
attributes.references: LIMS (LabWare); EPA 40 CFR Part 503; Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

tag_set.value: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Sample ID

attributes.name: primary_sludge_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the certified treatment plant operator who recorded or supervised the sludge production event. Supports regulatory compliance (operator certification requirements) and workforce accountability.
attributes.references: State Drinking Water Operator Certification Programs; OSHA; Water Utilities HR Standards

attributes.name: secondary_sludge_operator_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the certified treatment plant operator who recorded or supervised the sludge production event. Supports regulatory compliance (operator certification requirements) and workforce accountability.
attributes.references: State Drinking Water Operator Certification Programs; OSHA; Water Utilities HR Standards

attributes.name: primary_sludge_process_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific treatment process unit (e.g., clarifier, digester, filter) within the facility that generated the sludge. Sourced from OSIsoft PI Historian or IBM Maximo asset hierarchy.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: secondary_sludge_treatment_process_process_unit_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific treatment process unit (e.g., clarifier, digester, filter) within the facility that generated the sludge. Sourced from OSIsoft PI Historian or IBM Maximo asset hierarchy.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: treatment_permit_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Permit ID
attributes.description: Reference to the NPDES permit under which this sludge production event is reported. Required for Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) submissions to the EPA or state primacy agency.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Permit Program; Clean Water Act (CWA) Section 402

tag_set.value: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Permit ID

attributes.name: treatment_violation_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treatment.treatment_violation. Business justification: Sludge production records that fail biosolids compliance (metals_compliance, biosolids_class) generate treatment violations. This FK links sludge production records to the formal violation record for

attributes.name: biosolids_class
attributes.description: EPA biosolids quality classification under 40 CFR Part 503. 'Class_A' indicates pathogen reduction to below detectable levels (suitable for unrestricted land application); 'Class_B' indicates reduced but detectable pathogens (restricted land application with site restrictions); 'not_classified' for non-biosolids residuals such as alum or lime sludge.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503 Biosolids Rule; State Primacy Agency Biosolids Programs

attributes.name: bod_mg_per_l
attributes.description: Biochemical Oxygen Demand of the sludge liquor expressed in milligrams per liter (mg/L). Indicates organic loading returned to the treatment process via sludge liquors (reject water/filtrate). Sourced from LIMS analytical results.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503; SMEWW Method 5210B; NPDES DMR

attributes.name: cake_solids_pct
attributes.description: Solids content of the dewatered sludge cake expressed as a percentage by weight after dewatering. Indicates dewatering efficiency; higher values reduce disposal volume and cost. Applicable when a dewatering method is applied.
attributes.references: WEF Manual of Practice No. 8; EPA 40 CFR Part 503

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this sludge production record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Data Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: data_source
attributes.description: Identifies the originating operational system from which this sludge production record was sourced. Supports data lineage, quality assurance, and Silver Layer provenance tracking. Values: SCADA (OSIsoft PI Historian), LIMS (LabWare), manual_entry, CMMS (IBM Maximo), ERP (SAP).
attributes.references: Water Utilities Data Governance Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: dewatering_method
attributes.description: The mechanical or passive method used to reduce moisture content of the sludge prior to disposal. Options include centrifuge, belt press, filter press, drying beds, gravity thickener, or none (liquid sludge). Drives cake solids content and disposal cost.
attributes.references: WEF Manual of Practice No. 8; AWWA M20; EPA Biosolids Technology Fact Sheets

attributes.name: disposal_cost_usd
attributes.description: Total cost incurred for sludge disposal or beneficial use for this production event, expressed in US dollars. Includes hauling, tipping fees, and land application costs. Used for Operations and Maintenance (O&M) cost tracking, OPEX reporting, and Capital Improvement Program (CIP) planning.
attributes.references: GAAP; GASB Statement No. 34; SAP ERP FI/CO Module; Water Utilities Internal Finance Standards

attributes.name: disposal_date
attributes.description: Date on which the sludge was transported to and accepted at the disposal or beneficial use site. Used for manifest reconciliation and regulatory reporting period alignment.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503; NPDES DMR Reporting

attributes.name: disposal_manifest_number
attributes.description: Reference number of the waste disposal manifest or shipping document associated with the sludge disposal event. Required for chain-of-custody tracking and regulatory compliance under state solid waste and biosolids regulations.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503; State Solid Waste Regulations; RCRA Manifest Requirements

attributes.name: disposal_method
attributes.description: The final disposal or beneficial use pathway for the sludge or biosolids. Determines applicable regulatory requirements under EPA 40 CFR Part 503 and state biosolids programs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: landfill|land_application|incineration|composting|beneficial_reuse|co_disposal|surface_disposal — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503 Biosolids Rule; CWA Section 405; State Biosolids Programs

attributes.name: disposal_site_name
attributes.description: Name of the landfill, land application site, incineration facility, or composting facility receiving the sludge. Used for disposal tracking, permit compliance, and annual biosolids reporting.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503; State Biosolids Land Application Permits

attributes.name: dry_weight_tons
attributes.description: Dry solids weight of the sludge expressed in dry tons (US short tons). Calculated from volume and total solids concentration; used for biosolids land application permitting, disposal cost tracking, and EPA 40 CFR Part 503 annual reporting.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503 Biosolids Rule; NPDES Annual Biosolids Report

attributes.name: hauler_permit_number
attributes.description: State-issued waste transporter permit number for the sludge hauler. Required for regulatory compliance verification and manifest documentation under state solid waste and biosolids regulations.
attributes.references: State Solid Waste Transporter Regulations; EPA 40 CFR Part 503

attributes.name: is_biosolids_reportable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this sludge production event must be included in the EPA annual biosolids report (40 CFR Part 503) or state biosolids program report. True = reportable; False = exempt (e.g., alum sludge disposed to landfill under solid waste rules).
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503 Biosolids Rule; State Biosolids Programs

attributes.name: maximo_work_order_number
attributes.description: Work order number from IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS) associated with the dewatering or sludge handling maintenance activity. Supports Operations and Maintenance (O&M) cost tracking and asset performance management.
attributes.references: IBM Maximo Asset Management (CMMS); AWWA Asset Management Guidance

attributes.name: metals_compliance
attributes.description: Indicates whether the biosolids meet EPA 40 CFR Part 503 Table 1 ceiling concentration limits for regulated metals (arsenic, cadmium, copper, lead, mercury, molybdenum, nickel, selenium, zinc). True = all metals within ceiling limits; False = one or more exceedances detected. Sourced from LIMS metals analysis.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503.13 Pollutant Limits; LIMS (LabWare)

attributes.name: pathogen_reduction_method
attributes.description: The process used to reduce pathogen levels in biosolids to meet EPA 40 CFR Part 503 Class A or Class B requirements. Determines land application site restrictions and public access limitations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: anaerobic_digestion|aerobic_digestion|composting|heat_drying|lime_stabilization|alkaline_stabilization|none — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503 Biosolids Rule; WEF Manual of Practice No. 8

attributes.name: ph_value
attributes.description: pH measurement of the sludge at time of production or dewatering. Relevant for lime-stabilized biosolids (pH ≥ 12 required for Class A), corrosion control, and land application agronomic suitability. Sourced from LIMS.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503; SMEWW Method 4500-H+; LIMS (LabWare)

attributes.name: production_date
attributes.description: The calendar date on which sludge was generated or withdrawn from the treatment process. Principal business event date used for Monthly Operating Report (MOR) and DMR period aggregation.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES MOR/DMR Reporting Requirements; AWWA

attributes.name: production_number
attributes.description: Externally-known business identifier for this sludge production event, formatted as SLG-{YYYY}-{NNNNNN}. Used in residuals management logs, disposal manifests, and regulatory submissions.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Data Standards; EPA 40 CFR Part 503 Biosolids Rule

attributes.name: production_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the sludge production record. 'draft' indicates data entry in progress; 'confirmed' indicates volumes and quality data have been validated; 'disposed' indicates final disposal has been completed and manifested; 'cancelled' indicates the record was voided.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Data Standards; EPA 40 CFR Part 503

attributes.name: production_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when sludge generation or withdrawal was recorded, sourced from SCADA/OSIsoft PI Historian. Supports process analytics and shift-level reporting.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; AWWA M20 Water Chlorination/Chloramination Practices

attributes.name: remarks
attributes.description: Free-text field for operator or supervisor notes regarding the sludge production event, including process anomalies, equipment issues, sampling deviations, or regulatory observations. Supports MOR narrative sections.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES MOR Reporting; Water Utilities Internal Operations Standards

attributes.name: reporting_period
attributes.description: The calendar month and year (YYYY-MM) to which this sludge production record is attributed for Monthly Operating Report (MOR) and Discharge Monitoring Report (DMR) regulatory submissions. Ensures correct period alignment for compliance reporting.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES MOR/DMR Reporting Requirements; State Primacy Agency Reporting

attributes.name: scada_event_reference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Event Reference
attributes.description: Reference tag or event identifier from the OSIsoft PI Historian SCADA system corresponding to the sludge withdrawal or dewatering operation. Enables traceability between process control data and residuals management records.
attributes.references: OSIsoft PI Historian; SCADA Integration Standards

tag_set.value: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Event Reference

attributes.name: shift_code
attributes.description: Shift during which the sludge production event was recorded (day, evening, or night). Supports shift-level operational reporting, staffing analysis, and process performance benchmarking.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Operations Standards; OSHA

attributes.name: sludge_type
attributes.description: Classification of the sludge by its chemical or biological origin. 'alum_sludge' results from coagulation with aluminum sulfate; 'lime_sludge' from lime softening; 'biological_sludge' from activated sludge or biofilm processes at WWTPs; 'filter_backwash_solids' from filter media cleaning; 'mixed_sludge' from combined streams; 'digested_sludge' from anaerobic or aerobic digestion. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: alum_sludge|lime_sludge|biological_sludge|filter_backwash_solids|mixed_sludge|digested_sludge — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503 Biosolids Rule; AWWA M20; WEF Manual of Practice No. 8

attributes.name: total_solids_pct
attributes.description: Concentration of total solids in the sludge expressed as a percentage by weight (% TS). Key parameter for dewatering performance assessment and dry weight calculation. Sourced from LIMS analytical results.
attributes.references: Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater (SMEWW) Method 2540G; EPA 40 CFR Part 503

attributes.name: treatment_process
attributes.description: The specific water or wastewater treatment process that generated the sludge. Supports process-level residuals tracking and optimization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: coagulation|lime_softening|filtration|biological_treatment|anaerobic_digestion|aerobic_digestion|membrane_filtration|chemical_precipitation — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AWWA M36; WEF Manual of Practice No. 8; EPA Residuals Management Technical Guidance

attributes.name: tss_mg_per_l
attributes.description: Total Suspended Solids concentration in the sludge or associated liquor expressed in milligrams per liter (mg/L). Key parameter for NPDES permit compliance and process load calculations. Sourced from LIMS.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503; SMEWW Method 2540D; NPDES DMR

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this sludge production record was last modified. Supports change tracking and data quality auditing in the Silver Layer.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Data Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: vector_attraction_reduction
attributes.description: Indicates whether the sludge or biosolids meets vector attraction reduction (VAR) requirements under EPA 40 CFR Part 503.33. True = VAR requirements met; False = not met or not applicable. Required for land application permit compliance.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503.33 Vector Attraction Reduction

attributes.name: volatile_solids_pct
attributes.description: Percentage of volatile (organic) solids in the sludge relative to total solids. Indicates organic content and biological stability; used to assess vector attraction reduction compliance under EPA 40 CFR Part 503.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503 Biosolids Rule; SMEWW Method 2540E

attributes.name: volume_gallons
attributes.description: Volume of liquid sludge generated during the production event, measured in gallons. Primary quantitative measure for residuals management planning and NPDES permit compliance reporting.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503; NPDES DMR Reporting; AWWA

Supports chemical procurement planning, OSHA Tier II reporting, and treatment process continuity.

attributes.name: warehouse_location_id

attributes.name: average_daily_usage
attributes.description: Average quantity of the chemical consumed per day at the facility, expressed in the designated unit of measure. Calculated from historical dosing records and used to estimate days of supply remaining and optimize reorder frequency.

attributes.name: biosolids_permit_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this permit includes authorization for biosolids or residuals management (land application, incineration, or landfill disposal). Relevant for WWTPs subject to EPA 40 CFR Part 503 biosolids regulations.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 503 (Biosolids Standards); CWA Section 405; WEF

attributes.name: bod_limit_mg_l
attributes.description: Permitted maximum concentration of Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) in treated effluent, expressed in milligrams per liter (mg/L). A primary indicator of organic pollution load in wastewater discharge. Used for DMR compliance evaluation.
attributes.references: EPA Secondary Treatment Standards 40 CFR Part 133; CWA Section 301; NPDES Effluent Limitations

attributes.name: chlorine_residual_limit_mg_l
attributes.description: Minimum or maximum permitted chlorine residual concentration in finished water or treated effluent, expressed in mg/L. For drinking water, a minimum residual is required at the point of entry to the distribution system. For NPDES discharge, a maximum may be set to protect aquatic life.
attributes.references: SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.72 (Disinfection); EPA NPDES Aquatic Toxicity Limits; AWWA

attributes.name: compliance_schedule_end_date
attributes.description: The final date by which the facility must achieve full compliance with all permit limits per the regulatory-approved compliance schedule. Null if no compliance schedule is in effect. Used to track CIP project milestones and regulatory commitments.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.47; State Primacy Agency Compliance Schedule Requirements

attributes.name: compliance_schedule_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the permit includes a formal compliance schedule (a regulatory-approved timeline for achieving permit limits that the facility cannot currently meet). True triggers tracking of interim milestones and final compliance dates in the compliance management system.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.47 (Compliance Schedules); SDWA; State Primacy Agency Rules

attributes.name: ct_requirement_mg_min_l
attributes.description: Minimum required CT (Contact Time) value for disinfection as specified in the permit, expressed in mg·min/L (product of disinfectant concentration and contact time). CT compliance is a core Surface Water Treatment Rule requirement for Giardia and virus inactivation credit.
attributes.references: EPA Surface Water Treatment Rule (SWTR); LT2ESWTR; SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.72; CT Guidance Manual

attributes.name: dmr_submission_method
attributes.description: The required or preferred method for submitting Discharge Monitoring Reports (DMRs) or Monthly Operating Reports (MORs) to the regulatory agency. NetDMR is the EPA's electronic DMR system; eDMR refers to state-specific electronic systems; paper and state_portal are alternatives.
attributes.references: EPA NetDMR Program; 40 CFR Part 127 (NPDES Electronic Reporting Rule); State Primacy Agency

attributes.name: document_reference
attributes.description: Document management system reference, file path, or URL pointing to the official permit document, fact sheet, and associated attachments stored in the enterprise document repository. Enables direct access to the authoritative permit text for compliance review.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Document Management Policy; AWWA Compliance Records Management

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date on which the permit conditions become legally binding and enforceable. May differ from the issue date if a grace period or administrative continuance applies.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.21; State Primacy Agency Permit Conditions

attributes.name: expiration_date
attributes.description: The date on which the permit term expires. Triggers renewal workflow and compliance calendar alerts. Under administrative continuance provisions, operations may continue under the expired permit while renewal is pending.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.6 (Administrative Continuance); SDWA; CWA Section 402

attributes.name: facility_type
attributes.description: Classification of the treatment facility covered by this permit. Water Treatment Plant (WTP) produces finished drinking water; Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) or Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) treats and discharges wastewater; pump_station may hold ancillary permits; combined covers co-located facilities.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Program; SDWA; AWWA; WEF

attributes.name: haa5_mcl_ug_l
attributes.description: Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) for Haloacetic Acids (HAA5) as specified in the permit or applicable regulatory standard, expressed in micrograms per liter (µg/L). The EPA MCL for HAA5 is 60 µg/L. A key Disinfection Byproduct (DBP) compliance parameter for drinking water permits.
attributes.references: EPA Stage 2 DBPR; SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.64; HAA5 MCL

attributes.name: issue_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory agency formally issued or reissued the permit. Marks the start of the current permit term and is used to calculate permit age and renewal lead times.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Permit Administration; SDWA; CWA

attributes.name: last_inspection_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent regulatory compliance inspection conducted by the issuing agency or primacy agency at the permitted facility. Used to track inspection frequency, prepare for upcoming inspections, and assess compliance standing.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Compliance Inspection Program; SDWA Sanitary Survey Requirements; State Primacy Agency

attributes.name: monitoring_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency of effluent or finished water quality monitoring as specified in the permit. Drives the sampling schedule in the LIMS and the reporting calendar for DMR/MOR submissions. Represents the most frequent monitoring requirement across all parameters.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Monitoring Requirements; SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; State Primacy Agency Monitoring Plans

attributes.name: next_inspection_date
attributes.description: Anticipated or scheduled date of the next regulatory compliance inspection. Supports proactive compliance preparation and internal audit scheduling. May be estimated based on inspection frequency requirements.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Compliance Inspection Program; SDWA Sanitary Survey Schedule; State Primacy Agency

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional operational notes, regulatory correspondence summaries, internal compliance observations, or context not captured in structured fields. Used by compliance staff to document permit history, agency communications, and action items.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Compliance Management Policy; AWWA Compliance Records Management

attributes.name: npdes_major_minor_class
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Major/Minor Classification
attributes.description: EPA classification of the NPDES permit as major or minor based on facility size, discharge volume, and potential environmental impact. Major facilities are subject to more stringent oversight, mandatory DMR reporting, and EPA inspection priorities. Applicable only to NPDES permit types.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Program; 40 CFR Part 122; EPA ICIS-NPDES Classification Criteria

tag_set.value: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Major/Minor Classification

attributes.name: permit_category
attributes.description: Indicates whether the permit is an individual permit (facility-specific terms and conditions), a general permit (covers a category of similar dischargers), or an emergency permit (temporary authorization). Determines the regulatory review process and compliance obligations.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.28 (General Permits); SDWA; State Primacy Agency Rules

attributes.name: permit_name
attributes.description: Descriptive name or title of the permit as assigned by the issuing agency or used internally (e.g., 'City Water Treatment Plant NPDES Discharge Permit', 'Regional WTP Drinking Water Operating Permit'). Supports human-readable identification in compliance registers and reports.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Permit Register; AWWA Compliance Management Best Practices

attributes.name: permit_number
attributes.description: Externally-assigned permit number as issued by the regulatory authority (e.g., NPDES permit number, state drinking water operating permit number). This is the official identifier used in all regulatory correspondence, DMRs, MORs, and CCRs.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Program; SDWA; CWA; State Primacy Agency Permit Numbering

attributes.name: permit_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the permit. Active indicates the permit is in force; pending_renewal indicates the renewal application has been submitted and the permit is administratively continued; expired indicates the permit term has lapsed without renewal; suspended or revoked indicates regulatory action has been taken.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Permit Administration; SDWA Operating Permit Lifecycle; State Primacy Agency Rules

attributes.name: permit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the permit by regulatory program. NPDES governs wastewater discharge under the Clean Water Act; drinking_water_operating governs WTP operations under SDWA; air_emission covers process air releases; residuals_management covers biosolids/sludge disposal; industrial_pretreatment covers IUP programs; stormwater covers MS4 or industrial stormwater. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NPDES|drinking_water_operating|air_emission|residuals_management|industrial_pretreatment|stormwater|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: CWA Section 402 (NPDES); SDWA; EPA 40 CFR Parts 122-125; State Primacy Agency Regulations

attributes.name: permitted_avg_flow_mgd
attributes.business_glossary_term: Permitted Average Flow (Million Gallons per Day)
attributes.description: Monthly average flow rate authorized under this permit in Million Gallons per Day (MGD). Distinct from the peak daily limit; used for long-term capacity planning and average-basis compliance evaluation in DMR submissions.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Effluent Limitations Guidelines; 40 CFR Part 122 Appendix A

tag_set.value: Permitted Average Flow (Million Gallons per Day)

attributes.name: permitted_flow_mgd
attributes.description: Maximum daily flow rate authorized under this permit, expressed in Million Gallons per Day (MGD). This is the principal quantitative limit governing facility capacity and is used for capacity planning, compliance monitoring, and MOR/DMR reporting.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Effluent Limitations; SDWA Maximum Contaminant Levels; AWWA M1 Manual

attributes.name: pfas_monitoring_required
attributes.business_glossary_term: Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Monitoring Required Flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the permit requires monitoring for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) compounds. Reflects EPA's PFAS Action Plan and emerging state-level PFAS MCLs. Drives LIMS sampling plan configuration and CCR disclosure requirements.
attributes.references: EPA PFAS Action Plan; SDWA PFAS MCL Rule (2024); State PFAS Monitoring Requirements; AWWA

tag_set.value: Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Monitoring Required Flag

attributes.name: ph_limit_max
attributes.description: Maximum permitted pH value for treated effluent or finished water as specified in the permit. Used alongside ph_limit_min to define the acceptable pH range for compliance monitoring and corrosion control program evaluation.
attributes.references: EPA Secondary Treatment Standards; SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.21; NPDES Effluent Limitations

attributes.name: ph_limit_min
attributes.description: Minimum permitted pH value for treated effluent or finished water as specified in the permit. pH is a key indicator of water chemistry and corrosion control. Typically 6.0–9.0 for NPDES effluent; 6.5–8.5 for drinking water under SDWA.
attributes.references: EPA Secondary Treatment Standards; SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.21; NPDES Effluent Limitations

attributes.name: receiving_water_body
attributes.description: Name of the surface water body (river, lake, estuary, or ocean) designated as the receiving water for permitted discharges (e.g., 'Ohio River', 'Lake Michigan'). Required for NPDES permits; used in water quality impact assessments and antidegradation analysis.
attributes.references: CWA Section 303; EPA NPDES Permit Application; 40 CFR Part 131 (Water Quality Standards)

attributes.name: renewal_application_date
attributes.description: The date on which the permit renewal application was submitted to the issuing regulatory agency. NPDES regulations typically require submission at least 180 days before expiration. Used to verify timely renewal and administrative continuance eligibility.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.21(d); State Primacy Agency Renewal Requirements

attributes.name: renewal_status
attributes.description: Current status of the permit renewal process. Tracks progression from initial application through agency review to final determination. Supports compliance calendar management and regulatory relationship tracking.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Permit Renewal Process; SDWA Operating Permit Renewal; AWWA Compliance Management

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Required frequency for submitting compliance reports (DMRs, MORs, or equivalent) to the regulatory agency as specified in the permit. Drives the compliance reporting calendar and submission deadlines tracked in the MOR submission workflow.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES DMR Reporting Requirements; SDWA MOR Requirements; 40 CFR Part 122.41(l)

attributes.name: special_conditions
attributes.description: Narrative description of any special conditions, schedules of compliance, best management practices (BMPs), or additional requirements imposed by the regulatory agency beyond standard effluent limitations. Examples include PFAS monitoring requirements, CSO long-term control plan milestones, or LCRR service line inventory obligations.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES Permit Special Conditions; SDWA; LCRR; PFAS Action Plan; State Primacy Agency

attributes.name: term_years
attributes.description: Duration of the permit in years as specified by the issuing agency. NPDES permits are typically issued for 5-year terms; state drinking water operating permits may vary. Used for renewal planning and compliance scheduling.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 122.46 (NPDES 5-year term); SDWA; State Primacy Agency Rules

attributes.name: tss_limit_mg_l
attributes.description: Permitted maximum concentration of Total Suspended Solids (TSS) in treated effluent, expressed in milligrams per liter (mg/L). Core secondary treatment standard for WWTP NPDES compliance. Used in DMR reporting and effluent quality monitoring.
attributes.references: EPA Secondary Treatment Standards 40 CFR Part 133; CWA Section 301; NPDES Effluent Limitations

attributes.name: tthm_mcl_ug_l
attributes.description: Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) for Total Trihalomethanes (TTHMs) as specified in the permit or applicable regulatory standard, expressed in micrograms per liter (µg/L). The EPA MCL for TTHMs is 80 µg/L. A key Disinfection Byproduct (DBP) compliance parameter for drinking water permits.
attributes.references: EPA Stage 2 Disinfectants and Disinfection Byproducts Rule (Stage 2 DBPR); SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.64; MCL

attributes.name: turbidity_limit_ntu
attributes.description: Maximum permitted turbidity of finished water or treated effluent in Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU). For WTPs, the Surface Water Treatment Rule requires combined filter effluent turbidity not to exceed 0.3 NTU in 95% of measurements. Critical for MCL compliance.
attributes.references: EPA Surface Water Treatment Rule (SWTR); LT2ESWTR; 40 CFR Part 141.73; SDWA MCL

attributes.name: violation_count_active
attributes.description: Number of currently unresolved permit violations (effluent limit exceedances, reporting violations, or schedule of compliance violations) associated with this permit. Sourced from the regulatory agency's compliance tracking system. Used for compliance risk scoring and executive reporting.
attributes.references: EPA ECHO (Enforcement and Compliance History Online); NPDES Compliance Tracking; State Agency

products.name: chemical
products.description: Reference master for all chemicals used in treatment processes. Captures chemical name, common name, CAS number, chemical category (coagulant, disinfectant, pH adjuster, corrosion inhibitor, fluoridation agent, dechlorination agent, nutrient), approved supplier list, typical dose range (mg/L), maximum allowable dose (NSF/ANSI 60 certified), storage requirements, and regulatory approval status. Serves as the authoritative chemical catalog for treatment operations.
products.reference: NSF/ANSI 60 Drinking Water Treatment Chemical

attributes.description: Primary key for chemical

Captures violation type (MCL exceedance, treatment technique violation, monitoring and reporting violation, CT violation, turbidity violation), violation date, contaminant or parameter, measured value, regulatory limit, severity level, public notification requirement triggered, corrective action plan, resolution date, and regulatory agency notification status. Supports compliance management and public notification workflows.

attributes.name: general_ledger_id

attributes.name: primary_treatment_lab_sample_id
attributes.description: Laboratory sample identifier from the LIMS (LabWare or similar) that produced the analytical result triggering this violation. Enables traceability from violation back to the original lab sample and chain of custody.
attributes.references: LIMS (LabWare); EPA SDWA; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: process_reading_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to treatment.process_alarm. Business justification: Treatment violations are often triggered by process alarms (e.g., CT compliance failure, turbidity exceedance). The scada_alarm_tag string on treatment_violation should be replaced by FK to the treatm

attributes.name: regulatory_agency_id
attributes.description: Reference to the regulatory agency (e.g., EPA, State Primacy Agency) to which this violation must be reported.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: primary_treatment_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the certified treatment plant operator responsible for the process area at the time the violation was identified.
attributes.references: AWWA; State Drinking Water Operator Certification Programs

attributes.name: secondary_treatment_operator_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the certified treatment plant operator responsible for the process area at the time the violation was identified.
attributes.references: AWWA; State Drinking Water Operator Certification Programs

attributes.name: treatment_permit_id
attributes.business_glossary_term: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Permit ID
attributes.description: Reference to the NPDES permit under which the violation was recorded, applicable for wastewater discharge violations at WWTP facilities.
attributes.references: EPA CWA Section 402; NPDES Permit Program

tag_set.value: National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Permit ID

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Reference to the IBM Maximo CMMS work order created to execute the corrective action plan for this violation. Links compliance management to maintenance and operations workflows.

attributes.name: ccr_reportable
attributes.description: Indicates whether this violation must be disclosed in the annual Consumer Confidence Report (CCR) sent to customers, as required by EPA SDWA regulations for community water systems.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart O; Consumer Confidence Report Rule

attributes.name: contaminant_code
attributes.description: EPA or state-assigned contaminant code for the parameter that was violated (e.g., TTHM for Total Trihalomethanes, PFAS, turbidity, lead, copper, BOD, TSS). Aligns with EPA SDWIS contaminant codes.
attributes.references: EPA SDWIS Contaminant Code List; EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141

attributes.name: contaminant_name
attributes.description: Full descriptive name of the contaminant or treatment parameter involved in the violation (e.g., Total Trihalomethanes, Turbidity, Lead, Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS), Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD)).

attributes.name: corrective_action_due_date
attributes.description: The deadline by which the corrective action plan must be completed and compliance restored, as agreed with the regulatory agency or mandated by the compliance schedule.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency Compliance Schedules; AWWA

attributes.name: corrective_action_plan
attributes.description: Narrative description of the corrective action plan developed to address the root cause of the violation and restore compliance. Includes immediate remediation steps, process adjustments, and preventive measures.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; AWWA Compliance Management; ISO 14001 Environmental Management

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this violation record was first created in the compliance management system. Supports audit trail and data lineage requirements.
attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Data Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management; GASB

attributes.name: detection_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time when the violation was detected, either through SCADA/OSIsoft PI Historian alarm, laboratory result, or operator observation. Supports CT compliance and public notification deadline calculations.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141.85; OSIsoft PI Historian

attributes.name: dmr_reporting_period
attributes.description: The DMR reporting period (YYYY-MM) in which this violation must be included for NPDES permit compliance reporting. Applicable for WWTP effluent violations. Links to the corresponding DMR submission.

attributes.name: enforcement_action_taken
attributes.description: Indicates whether the regulatory agency has initiated a formal enforcement action (e.g., Notice of Violation, Administrative Order, Consent Order, penalty) in response to this violation.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; EPA Enforcement and Compliance Assurance; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: enforcement_action_type
attributes.description: Type of formal enforcement action taken by the regulatory agency (e.g., Notice of Violation (NOV), Administrative Order (AO), Consent Order, Civil Penalty, Criminal Referral). Null if no enforcement action was taken. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: NOV|administrative_order|consent_order|civil_penalty|criminal_referral|compliance_schedule|none — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; EPA Enforcement and Compliance Assurance; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: exceedance_magnitude
attributes.description: The numeric difference between the measured value and the regulatory limit (measured_value minus regulatory_limit). Positive values indicate the degree of exceedance above the limit, supporting severity assessment and trend analysis.

attributes.name: facility_type
attributes.description: Type of treatment facility where the violation occurred: WTP (Water Treatment Plant), WWTP (Wastewater Treatment Plant), STP (Sewage Treatment Plant), booster station, or storage facility.

attributes.name: is_repeat_violation
attributes.description: Indicates whether this violation is a repeat occurrence of the same contaminant or parameter violation at the same facility within the preceding 12-month period. Repeat violations may trigger escalated regulatory response and increased penalties.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency Programs; AWWA Compliance Analytics

attributes.name: measured_value
attributes.description: The actual measured concentration, level, or parameter value recorded at the time of the violation (e.g., turbidity in NTU, chlorine residual in mg/L, BOD in mg/L, CT value in mg·min/L). This is the quantitative result that triggered the violation.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; EPA NPDES; LIMS (LabWare)

attributes.name: measured_value_uom
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the measured_value field (e.g., mg/L for chemical concentrations, NTU for Nephelometric Turbidity Units, mg·min/L for CT Contact Time, CFU/100mL for microbial counts). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg/L|NTU|mg·min/L|CFU/100mL|pH|mg/kg|ug/L|pCi/L|MPN/100mL — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; AWWA; ISO 9001

attributes.name: mor_reporting_period
attributes.description: The MOR reporting period (YYYY-MM) in which this violation must be included for regulatory submission. Links the violation to the corresponding Monthly Operating Report for the facility.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency MOR Requirements; AWWA

attributes.name: operator_notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for the certified treatment plant operator to record observations, circumstances, and contextual information about the violation at the time of detection or during investigation.
attributes.references: AWWA; State Drinking Water Operator Certification Programs

attributes.name: penalty_amount
attributes.description: Monetary penalty assessed by the regulatory agency for this violation, in USD. Supports financial liability tracking, OPEX reporting, and GAAP/GASB financial disclosures for municipal utilities.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; GAAP; GASB; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: permit_number
attributes.description: The operating permit number (e.g., NPDES permit number, state drinking water permit) under which the facility operates and against which the violation is recorded. Used in regulatory correspondence and DMR/MOR submissions.
attributes.references: EPA NPDES; EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: process_area
attributes.description: The specific treatment process area or unit operation where the violation originated (e.g., coagulation, filtration, UV disinfection, chlorination, RO, UF, MF, GAC, sedimentation, aeration, biological treatment).
attributes.references: AWWA; WEF; OSIsoft PI Historian Process Tags

attributes.name: public_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which public notification was issued to customers and the public in accordance with the EPA Public Notification Rule. Null if notification has not yet been issued.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Q; Oracle Utilities CC&B

attributes.name: public_notification_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether this violation triggers a mandatory public notification requirement under EPA SDWA Public Notification Rule (40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Q). True when the violation type and severity mandate customer and public notification.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Q; Public Notification Rule

attributes.name: public_notification_tier
attributes.description: EPA Public Notification Rule tier classification: Tier 1 requires notification within 24 hours (acute health risk); Tier 2 requires notification within 30 days; Tier 3 requires annual notification. Drives notification workflow and deadline management.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141 Subpart Q; Public Notification Rule

attributes.name: regulatory_limit
attributes.description: The applicable Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL), treatment technique standard, or permit limit that was exceeded or violated. For CT violations, this is the required CT value in mg·min/L.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; EPA NPDES; AWWA; LCRR

attributes.name: regulatory_limit_type
attributes.description: Classification of the regulatory standard that was violated: MCL (Maximum Contaminant Level), MCLG (Maximum Contaminant Level Goal), treatment technique standard, NPDES permit limit, action level (e.g., Lead and Copper Rule), or required CT (Contact Time for Disinfection).
attributes.references: EPA SDWA 40 CFR Part 141; EPA NPDES; LCRR; AWWA

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_date
attributes.description: The date on which the regulatory agency (EPA or State Primacy Agency) was formally notified of this violation, as required by SDWA or NPDES permit conditions.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; EPA NPDES; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: regulatory_notification_status
attributes.description: Status of the formal notification to the regulatory agency (EPA or State Primacy Agency) regarding this violation. Tracks whether notification is pending, has been submitted, has been acknowledged, or is overdue per regulatory deadlines.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; State Primacy Agency Programs; NACWA

attributes.name: resolution_date
attributes.description: The date on which the violation was resolved and compliance was restored, confirmed by a return-to-compliance sample result or regulatory acknowledgment. Null if the violation remains open.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; AWWA; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: root_cause_category
attributes.description: Categorical classification of the root cause of the violation to support trend analysis and preventive action programs. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: equipment_failure|process_upset|operator_error|source_water_event|chemical_dosing|monitoring_failure|reporting_failure|infrastructure|other — promote to reference product]
attributes.references: AWWA; WEF; ISO 14001 Environmental Management; ISO 9001 Quality Management

attributes.name: severity_level
attributes.description: Assessed severity classification of the violation based on the degree of exceedance, public health risk, and regulatory consequence. Critical indicates immediate public health risk; high indicates significant exceedance; medium indicates moderate concern; low indicates minor or administrative violation.
attributes.references: EPA SDWA; AWWA Compliance Management Best Practices; State Primacy Agency Programs

attributes.name: updated_timestamp

attributes.references: Water Utilities Internal Data Standards; ISO 9001 Quality Management; GASB

attributes.name: violation_date

attributes.name: violation_number
attributes.description: Externally-known, human-readable unique reference number assigned to this violation record, used in regulatory correspondence, public notifications, and compliance tracking systems.
