attributes.name: mclg
attributes.description: The Maximum Contaminant Level Goal (MCLG) - the level of a contaminant in drinking water below which there is no known or expected risk to health. MCLGs are non-enforceable public health goals. Value of zero indicates no safe level. Null indicates no MCLG established.
attributes.references: Safe Drinking Water Act Section 1412(b)(4), 40 CFR 141.153(d)(4)(iii)

attributes.name: modified_timestamp

attributes.name: monitoring_period_start_date
attributes.description: The beginning date of the monitoring period for which this contaminant detection data was collected. Defines the temporal scope of the reported results.

attributes.name: number_of_detections
attributes.description: Count of samples in which this contaminant was detected above the method detection limit (MDL) or practical quantitation level (PQL) during the reporting period. Provides transparency on detection frequency.

attributes.name: number_of_samples
attributes.description: Total count of samples collected and analyzed for this contaminant during the reporting period. Used to demonstrate compliance with monitoring frequency requirements and provide context for detection statistics.

attributes.name: public_notification_required_flag

attributes.name: range_low
attributes.description: The lowest level detected for this contaminant across all samples collected during the reporting period. Forms the lower bound of the detection range required for CCR reporting. May be zero or below detection limit.

attributes.name: regulatory_program

products.name: territory_contaminant_monitoring_requirement
products.description: This association product represents the territory-specific monitoring requirements and regulatory variances between contaminants and service territories. It captures jurisdiction-specific monitoring frequencies, action levels, and variance statuses that exist only in the context of a specific contaminant being monitored within a specific service territory. Each record links one contaminant to one service territory with regulatory override attributes that reflect primacy agency decisions, vulnerability assessments, and approved variances.. Existence Justification: In water utility operations, contaminants have different monitoring requirements across service territories based on primacy agency jurisdiction, source water vulnerability assessments, and approved regulatory variances. A single contaminant (e.g., lead) may require quarterly monitoring in one territory but have a waiver for reduced frequency in another territory based on vulnerability assessment results. Conversely, a single service territory must track territory-specific monitoring requirements, action levels, and variance statuses for dozens of regulated contaminants. This is an operational compliance management relationship that utilities actively maintain.

attributes.name: dilution_factor
attributes.description: Multiplier applied to raw instrument response to account for sample dilution performed to bring analyte concentration within instrument calibration range. A value of 1.0 indicates no dilution.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp

attributes.name: matrix_type
attributes.description: Classification of the sample medium being analyzed. Matrix type affects method selection, quality control requirements, and regulatory applicability. attributes.name: percent_recovery
attributes.description: Quality control metric indicating the percentage of known analyte concentration recovered in matrix spike or laboratory control sample. Used to assess method accuracy and matrix interference. Acceptable ranges are method-specific.
attributes.references: EPA QA/QC requirements, ISO/IEC 17025 - Accuracy verification

attributes.name: preservation_method
attributes.description: Chemical or physical treatment applied to the sample to maintain analyte stability during storage and transport (e.g., acidification with HNO3, refrigeration at 4°C, addition of sodium thiosulfate for dechlorination).

attributes.name: qualifier_code
attributes.description: Data quality flag indicating special conditions affecting the result. U=non-detect (below detection limit), J=estimated value (between MDL and RL), B=blank contamination detected, E=exceeds calibration range, H=hold time exceeded, N=tentative identification, Q=QC failure, R=rejected, S=spike recovery out of range, T=temperature exceedance, V=value verified, X=other (see comments). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: U|J|B|E|H|N|Q|R|S|T|V|X — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA Contract Laboratory Program (CLP) data qualifier definitions, NELAC Institute standards

attributes.name: raw_instrument_response
attributes.description: Uncorrected measurement value directly from the analytical instrument before applying dilution factors, calibration curves, or other corrections. Retained for audit trails and method validation.

attributes.name: reanalysis_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the test must be repeated due to quality control failure, questionable results, or regulatory requirements. Triggers workflow to schedule reanalysis from the same sample or request new sample collection.

attributes.name: regulatory_program
attributes.description: Federal or state regulatory program under which this test is being performed. Determines applicable compliance thresholds, reporting requirements, and data quality objectives. SDWA=Safe Drinking Water Act, CWA=Clean Water Act, NPDES=National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System. attributes.name: rejection_reason
attributes.description: Detailed explanation for why the test result was rejected and cannot be used for regulatory reporting. Common reasons include QC failure, hold time exceedance, contamination, instrument malfunction, or analyst error. Triggers resampling or reanalysis.

attributes.name: relative_percent_difference
attributes.description: Quality control metric measuring precision between duplicate samples. Calculated as the absolute difference divided by the mean, expressed as a percentage. Used to assess analytical reproducibility.
attributes.references: EPA QA/QC requirements, ISO/IEC 17025 - Precision verification

attributes.name: reporting_limit
attributes.description: Minimum concentration that can be reliably quantified and reported. Typically set at 2-10 times the Method Detection Limit (MDL) to ensure data quality and regulatory compliance.
attributes.references: EPA Practical Quantitation Limit (PQL) guidance, ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: result_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the result value (e.g., mg/L, ug/L, NTU, MPN/100mL, pH units, CFU/100mL). Must align with regulatory reporting requirements and Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) units.
attributes.references: EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations (NPDWR), Standard Methods

attributes.name: result_value
attributes.description: Calculated analytical result value after applying dilution factors, calibration curves, and method-specific calculations. This is the reportable concentration or measurement for the analyte.

attributes.name: review_timestamp

attributes.name: compliance_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the result meets applicable regulatory thresholds. Values: compliant (result within acceptable limits), non-compliant (result exceeds Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL) or violates National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) limit), exceedance (result exceeds action level but not MCL), not_applicable (no regulatory threshold for this parameter), pending_review (compliance determination not yet made).
attributes.references: Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA), Clean Water Act (CWA), EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this test result record was first created in the system. Represents the initial capture of the result data.

attributes.name: detection_status
attributes.description: Indicates whether the analyte was detected in the sample. Values: detected (analyte present above Method Detection Limit), non-detect (analyte not detected or below MDL), trace (analyte detected but below quantitation limit), below_mdl (result below Method Detection Limit), above_mdl (result above Method Detection Limit and quantifiable).
attributes.references: EPA Method Detection Limit (MDL) procedures (40 CFR Part 136, Appendix B)

attributes.name: dilution_factor
attributes.description: The factor by which the sample was diluted prior to analysis. A value of 1.0 indicates no dilution. Values greater than 1.0 indicate the sample was diluted to bring analyte concentration within the calibration range or to reduce matrix interference.
attributes.references: Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater, laboratory Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)

attributes.name: duplicate_relative_percent_difference
attributes.description: Relative percent difference between the sample result and its duplicate, calculated as (|Sample - Duplicate| / Average) × 100. Indicates the precision of the analytical method. Acceptable ranges are method-specific (typically <20%).
attributes.references: EPA Quality Assurance/Quality Control guidelines, method-specific acceptance criteria

attributes.name: holding_time_compliance_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the sample was analyzed within the method-specified holding time (time between sample collection and analysis). True indicates compliance; False indicates holding time was exceeded, which may affect result validity.
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 136, EPA sample preservation and holding time requirements

attributes.name: lims_result_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Result ID
attributes.description: The unique result identifier from the source Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS), such as LabWare. Enables traceability back to the originating system and supports data reconciliation.

tag_set.value: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Result ID

attributes.name: matrix_spike_recovery_percent
attributes.description: Percent recovery of the analyte from the matrix spike sample analyzed in the same batch. Indicates the accuracy of the method in the presence of the sample matrix. Acceptable ranges are method-specific (typically 75-125%).
attributes.references: EPA Quality Assurance/Quality Control guidelines, method-specific acceptance criteria

attributes.name: method_detection_limit
attributes.description: The minimum concentration of an analyte that can be measured and reported with 99% confidence that the value is greater than zero. Specific to the test method and laboratory instrumentation used.
attributes.references: 40 CFR Part 136, Appendix B - Definition and Procedure for the Determination of the Method Detection Limit

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when this test result record was last modified. Tracks any updates to the result data after initial creation.

attributes.name: proficiency_test_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this result is from a proficiency testing (PT) sample used to evaluate laboratory performance. True indicates this is a PT result; False indicates a routine sample result.

attributes.name: reanalysis_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this result is from a reanalysis of the sample. True indicates the sample was reanalyzed due to quality control failure, holding time exceedance, or other issue with the initial analysis; False indicates this is the first analysis.

attributes.name: regulatory_threshold_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the regulatory threshold value. Must be compatible with the reporting_unit to enable valid comparison. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg/L|ug/L|NTU|CFU/100mL|MPN/100mL|pH units|percent|ppm|ppb|SU — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA), Clean Water Act (CWA), EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations

attributes.name: regulatory_threshold_value
attributes.description: The applicable regulatory limit against which this result is compared (e.g., Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL), Maximum Contaminant Level Goal (MCLG), National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) effluent limit). Captured at the time of result approval to preserve the threshold in effect.
attributes.references: Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA), Clean Water Act (CWA), EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations

attributes.name: reporting_limit
attributes.description: The minimum concentration at which the laboratory can quantitatively report a result with confidence. Typically set at 2-10 times the Method Detection Limit (MDL). Also known as Practical Quantitation Limit (PQL) or Limit of Quantitation (LOQ).
attributes.references: EPA Quality Assurance/Quality Control guidelines, ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: reporting_timestamp
attributes.description: Date and time when the result was officially reported to the client or regulatory agency. Distinct from approval_timestamp which is internal laboratory validation; this marks external release.

attributes.name: reporting_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure in which the result value is reported. Common units include milligrams per liter (mg/L), micrograms per liter (ug/L), Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU), Colony Forming Units per 100 milliliters (CFU/100mL), Most Probable Number per 100 milliliters (MPN/100mL), pH units, percent, parts per million (ppm), parts per billion (ppb), Standard Units (SU). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg/L|ug/L|NTU|CFU/100mL|MPN/100mL|pH units|percent|ppm|ppb|SU — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater, EPA reporting requirements

attributes.name: result_comment
attributes.description: Free-text comment field for analyst notes, observations, or explanations regarding the result. May include information about matrix interference, unusual sample characteristics, deviations from standard procedure, or other contextual information.

attributes.name: result_qualifier
attributes.description: Data qualifier code providing additional context about the result (e.g., J=estimated value, U=undetected, E=exceeds calibration range, B=blank contamination, H=holding time exceeded, Q=quality control failure). Follows EPA and laboratory-specific qualifier conventions.
attributes.references: EPA Contract Laboratory Program (CLP) data qualifiers, laboratory-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs)

attributes.name: result_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the result record. Values: final (result approved and released), preliminary (result generated but not yet approved), rejected (result failed quality control and is not valid), under_review (result pending analyst review), cancelled (result voided due to sample or procedural issue).

attributes.name: result_value
attributes.description: The validated and finalized numeric result value reported from the analytical test. This is the authoritative measurement released for compliance and operational use.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025, EPA Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) guidelines

attributes.name: uncertainty_estimate
attributes.description: Quantitative estimate of the uncertainty associated with the reported result, expressed in the same units as the result. Represents the range within which the true value is expected to lie with a specified confidence level (typically 95%).
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025, EURACHEM/CITAC Guide on Measurement Uncertainty

attributes.name: instrument_name

attributes.name: lab_location

attributes.name: last_calibration_date

attributes.name: lims_instrument_code

attributes.name: manufacturer

attributes.name: measurement_range_max
attributes.description: Upper bound of the instrument's measurement range, expressed in the instrument's native units. For example, 1000 mg/L for an ICP-MS, or 1000 NTU for a turbidimeter. Values beyond this range require dilution or alternative methods.

attributes.name: measurement_range_min
attributes.description: Lower bound of the instrument's measurement range or detection limit, expressed in the instrument's native units. For example, 0.001 mg/L for an ICP-MS measuring trace metals, or 0.1 NTU for a turbidimeter.
attributes.references: AWWA Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: measurement_unit
attributes.description: Standard unit of measure for results produced by this instrument (e.g., 'mg/L', 'ug/L', 'NTU', 'pH units', 'uS/cm', 'mg/L as CaCO3'). Must align with regulatory reporting requirements and laboratory LIMS (Laboratory Information Management System) configuration.
attributes.references: AWWA Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: model_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer's model number or designation for the instrument, used for parts ordering, service manuals, and technical specifications.

attributes.name: next_calibration_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next required calibration event, calculated based on calibration frequency requirements and last calibration date. Instruments past due for calibration must be taken out of service per ISO/IEC 17025.

attributes.name: next_maintenance_due_date
attributes.description: Scheduled date for the next preventive maintenance activity, calculated based on maintenance frequency and last maintenance date. Used for work order scheduling in CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management System).

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional information about the instrument, including special handling requirements, known quirks, configuration details, or historical context not captured in structured fields.

attributes.name: operational_status
attributes.description: Current operational state of the instrument. In Service indicates the instrument is available and qualified for testing. Out of Service indicates temporary unavailability. attributes.name: primary_test_method

attributes.name: purchase_cost
attributes.description: Original acquisition cost of the instrument in USD, used for asset valuation, depreciation calculations, and capital budgeting. Excludes installation and training costs unless capitalized.

attributes.name: purchase_date
attributes.description: Date the instrument was purchased or acquired by the organization, used for warranty tracking and capital expenditure (CAPEX) reporting.

attributes.name: retirement_date
attributes.description: Date the instrument was permanently retired from service and removed from the active laboratory inventory. Used for asset disposal tracking and historical record keeping.

attributes.name: retirement_reason
attributes.description: Explanation for why the instrument was retired (e.g., 'End of useful life', 'Replaced by newer model', 'Excessive repair costs', 'Obsolete technology', 'Regulatory method discontinued'). Used for asset lifecycle analysis and replacement planning.

attributes.name: secondary_test_methods
attributes.description: Comma-separated list of additional test methods or Standard Method numbers that this instrument can perform, beyond the primary method. Used for multi-parameter instruments or instruments with multiple configurations.
attributes.references: AWWA Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: serial_number
attributes.description: Manufacturer-assigned unique serial number for this specific instrument unit, used for warranty claims, service history, and regulatory traceability.

attributes.name: service_contract_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date the current vendor service contract expires, after which service calls will be billed separately or a new contract must be negotiated. Used for budgeting and contract renewal planning.

attributes.name: updated_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this instrument record was last modified, used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization with source systems.

attributes.name: warranty_expiration_date
attributes.description: Date the manufacturer's warranty coverage expires, after which repairs and parts are at the organization's expense. Used for maintenance planning and service contract decisions.

products.name: laboratory_instrument_calibration
products.description: Transactional record of each instrument calibration event performed in the laboratory. Captures calibration type (initial, continuing, multi-point, single-point), calibration standard used, standard lot number and expiry, calibration curve coefficients, acceptance criteria (R² threshold, percent recovery), pass/fail result, calibration datetime, analyst performing calibration, and next calibration due date. Required for data defensibility under NELAC/TNI accreditation and EPA method requirements.
products.reference: Instrument Calibration Log (LabWare / NELAC TNI Standard)

attributes.name: laboratory_instrument_calibration_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the laboratory_instrument_calibration data product (auto-inserted pre-linking).

attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.certified_analyst. Business justification: Calibration events are performed BY certified analysts. This N:1 relationship (many calibrations per analyst) tracks who performed the calibration, which is required for regulatory traceability and qu

attributes.name: lab_instrument_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to laboratory.lab_instrument. Business justification: Calibration events are performed ON specific laboratory instruments. This is a core N:1 relationship (many calibration events per instrument). The FK enables tracking of calibration history per instru

products.name: qc_batch
products.description: Quality control batch record grouping a set of analytical tests processed together under the same QC conditions. Defines the batch type (preparation batch, analytical batch), associated test method, batch size, batch preparation datetime, analyst, and the QC samples included (method blank, laboratory control sample, matrix spike, matrix spike duplicate, surrogate). Tracks overall batch acceptance status based on QC acceptance criteria and is the primary unit for QC review and data validation in the laboratory. Batch failure triggers corrective action and may require re-analysis of all associated samples.
products.reference: QC Batch / Analytical Batch (EPA QA/QC Requirements / NELAC TNI)

attributes.name: qc_batch_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the quality control batch record. Primary key.

attributes.name: certified_analyst_id
attributes.description: Reference to the certified laboratory analyst who performed the analytical work for this batch. Ensures traceability and accountability for test results.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: QC batch costs (reference standards, control samples, analyst time) represent laboratory overhead that must be allocated to a cost center for overhead rate calculation and indirect cost distribution.

attributes.name: lab_instrument_id
attributes.description: Reference to the analytical instrument used for this batch. Links to instrument calibration records and maintenance history.

attributes.name: primary_qc_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the laboratory supervisor or QA officer who reviewed and approved the batch QC results. Ensures accountability for data validation decisions.

attributes.name: secondary_reviewer_employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the laboratory supervisor or QA officer who reviewed and approved the batch QC results. Ensures accountability for data validation decisions.

attributes.name: test_method_id
attributes.description: Reference to the analytical test method applied to all samples in this QC batch. Ensures all samples are processed under the same standardized procedure.
attributes.references: EPA Methods, AWWA Standard Methods for Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: batch_completion_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when all analytical work for the batch was completed and results were recorded. Used to calculate batch processing time and ensure timely reporting.

attributes.name: batch_number
attributes.description: Human-readable unique batch identifier assigned by the laboratory information management system (LIMS). Used for tracking and referencing in laboratory documentation and chain of custody records.

attributes.name: batch_preparation_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the batch preparation or analytical run was initiated. Critical for hold time compliance and method-specific timing requirements.

attributes.name: batch_review_datetime
attributes.description: Date and time when the QC batch was reviewed and acceptance status was assigned by the laboratory supervisor or quality assurance officer.

attributes.name: batch_size
attributes.description: Total number of samples (including field samples and QC samples) processed together in this batch. Used to verify batch integrity and compliance with method-specific batch size limits.

attributes.name: batch_type
attributes.description: Classification of the QC batch based on the laboratory process stage. Preparation batch groups samples undergoing initial preparation; analytical batch groups samples analyzed together under identical conditions; extraction/digestion batches are specific to sample matrix processing.

attributes.name: corrective_action_required
attributes.description: Indicates whether QC failures or deviations in this batch require formal corrective action per laboratory quality management system. Triggers corrective action workflow.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this QC batch record was first created in the data system. Part of audit trail for data lineage and compliance.

attributes.name: duplicate_acceptance_status
attributes.description: QC acceptance status for the duplicate sample based on RPD limits. Fail status may indicate sample heterogeneity or analytical imprecision.

attributes.name: duplicate_relative_percent_difference
attributes.description: Calculated RPD between original and duplicate field samples. Measures precision of the entire analytical process including sample heterogeneity.

attributes.name: duplicate_sample_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether a duplicate field sample was analyzed in this batch. Duplicates assess overall analytical precision for unspiked samples.

attributes.name: field_sample_count
attributes.description: Number of actual field samples (non-QC samples) included in this batch. Excludes method blanks, laboratory control samples, and other QC samples.

attributes.name: lcs_acceptance_status
attributes.description: QC acceptance status for the LCS based on percent recovery limits. Fail status indicates systematic bias and may require corrective action or batch reanalysis.

attributes.name: lcs_expected_value
attributes.description: Known or true concentration of the analyte in the laboratory control sample. Used to calculate percent recovery.

attributes.name: lcs_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether a laboratory control sample was included in this batch. LCS is a known-concentration standard used to verify method accuracy and instrument performance.

attributes.name: lcs_measured_value
attributes.description: Analytical result obtained for the laboratory control sample. Compared against expected value to calculate percent recovery.

attributes.name: lcs_percent_recovery
attributes.description: Calculated percent recovery for the LCS: (measured_value / expected_value) * 100. Must fall within method-specific acceptance limits (typically 80-120%) to validate batch accuracy.

attributes.name: lims_batch_code
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Batch Identifier
attributes.description: External batch identifier from the laboratory information management system (LabWare or similar). Used for integration and cross-system traceability.

tag_set.value: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Batch Identifier

attributes.name: matrix_spike_acceptance_status
attributes.description: QC acceptance status for the matrix spike based on percent recovery limits. Fail status may indicate matrix interference requiring method modification or result qualification.

attributes.name: matrix_spike_duplicate_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether a matrix spike duplicate was included in this batch. MSD is a second spiked aliquot of the same sample used to assess analytical precision through relative percent difference (RPD) calculation.

attributes.name: matrix_spike_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether a matrix spike sample was included in this batch. Matrix spike is a field sample spiked with known analyte concentration to assess matrix interference and method accuracy in real sample matrices.

attributes.name: matrix_spike_percent_recovery
attributes.description: Calculated percent recovery for the matrix spike. Evaluates the effect of sample matrix on analytical accuracy. Acceptance limits are method-specific.

attributes.name: method_blank_acceptance_status
attributes.description: QC acceptance status for the method blank based on method-specific criteria. Fail status indicates contamination and may require batch reanalysis.

attributes.name: method_blank_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether a method blank (reagent blank) was included in this batch. Method blanks are required to detect contamination from reagents, glassware, or the analytical process.
attributes.references: EPA Quality Assurance, AWWA Standard Methods

attributes.name: method_blank_result
attributes.description: Analytical result for the method blank. Should be below the method detection limit (MDL) to confirm no contamination. Elevated blank results may invalidate the entire batch.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this QC batch record was last modified. Tracks data changes for audit and quality assurance purposes.

attributes.name: msd_acceptance_status
attributes.description: QC acceptance status for the MSD based on RPD limits. Fail status indicates poor precision and may require investigation or reanalysis.

attributes.name: msd_percent_recovery
attributes.description: Calculated percent recovery for the matrix spike duplicate. Used in conjunction with MS recovery to calculate relative percent difference.

attributes.name: msd_relative_percent_difference
attributes.business_glossary_term: Matrix Spike Duplicate (MSD) Relative Percent Difference (RPD)
attributes.description: Calculated RPD between matrix spike and matrix spike duplicate: |MS - MSD| / ((MS + MSD) / 2) * 100. Measures analytical precision; must meet method-specific limits (typically <20%).

tag_set.value: Matrix Spike Duplicate (MSD) Relative Percent Difference (RPD)

attributes.name: overall_batch_acceptance_status
attributes.description: Final QC acceptance status for the entire batch based on all QC sample results. Accepted batches have all QC criteria met; rejected batches require reanalysis; conditional batches may have qualified results.

attributes.name: qc_comments
attributes.description: Free-text field for documenting QC issues, corrective actions taken, deviations from standard procedures, or explanations for conditional acceptance. Critical for audit trail and regulatory compliance.

attributes.name: surrogate_acceptance_status
attributes.description: QC acceptance status for surrogate standards based on recovery limits. Fail status may indicate sample preparation problems or matrix interference.

attributes.name: surrogate_included
attributes.description: Indicates whether surrogate standards were added to all samples in this batch. Surrogates are analyte-like compounds added before sample processing to monitor extraction and analytical efficiency.

attributes.name: surrogate_percent_recovery
attributes.description: Average percent recovery for surrogate standards across the batch. Used to assess sample preparation and extraction efficiency. Method-specific acceptance limits apply.
attributes.references: EPA Organic Analysis Methods, Quality Assurance

products.name: qc_sample
products.description: Record for each quality control sample included in a QC batch. Captures QC sample type (method blank, laboratory control sample LCS, matrix spike MS, matrix spike duplicate MSD, field duplicate, field blank, surrogate spike, certified reference material CRM), expected concentration, measured concentration, percent recovery, relative percent difference RPD, acceptance limits, and pass/fail status. Provides the QA/QC evidence trail required for data validation and laboratory accreditation.
products.reference: QC Sample / QA Check (NELAC TNI Standard / EPA Method QC Requirements)

attributes.name: qc_sample_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the quality control sample record. Primary key.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - General requirements for the competence of testing and calibration laboratories

attributes.name: analyte_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific analyte or parameter being measured in this QC sample (e.g., lead, chlorine, pH, Total Organic Carbon (TOC), Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD)).
attributes.references: EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations; Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA)

attributes.name: lab_instrument_id
attributes.description: Reference to the laboratory instrument used for this QC sample analysis. Links to instrument calibration and maintenance records.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - Equipment calibration and maintenance requirements

attributes.name: lab_sample_id
attributes.description: Reference to the associated environmental or production sample when applicable (e.g., for matrix spike or field duplicate QC types). Null for method blanks and laboratory control samples.
attributes.references: EPA Method 200.7 - Sample preparation and QC requirements

attributes.name: primary_qc_certified_analyst_id
attributes.description: Reference to the certified laboratory analyst who performed the QC sample analysis. Required for chain of custody and accreditation compliance.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - Personnel competence requirements; State laboratory certification programs

attributes.name: qc_batch_id
attributes.description: Reference to the QC batch that contains this QC sample. Links to the parent batch for traceability.

attributes.name: test_method_id
attributes.description: Reference to the analytical test method applied to this QC sample. Links to the standard operating procedure and method specifications.
attributes.references: EPA approved methods; AWWA Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: accreditation_body
attributes.description: Name of the accreditation body or state certification program under which this QC sample was analyzed (e.g., state drinking water laboratory certification program, NELAP, A2LA). Required for regulatory reporting and audit trail.
attributes.references: EPA National Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (NELAP); State laboratory certification programs; ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: analysis_date
attributes.description: Date the QC sample was analyzed in the laboratory. Used to verify compliance with method-specific holding time requirements and to track batch chronology.
attributes.references: EPA Method 200.7; ISO/IEC 17025 - Record keeping requirements

attributes.name: analysis_timestamp
attributes.description: Precise date and time the QC sample analysis was completed. Provides detailed audit trail for Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) integration and regulatory reporting.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - Traceability and record keeping; LabWare LIMS data model

attributes.name: concentration_unit
attributes.description: Unit of measure for the expected and measured concentration values. Common units include milligrams per liter (mg/L), micrograms per liter (ug/L), nanograms per liter (ng/L), parts per million (ppm), parts per billion (ppb), parts per trillion (ppt), Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU), Colony Forming Units per 100 milliliters (CFU/100mL), Most Probable Number per 100 milliliters (MPN/100mL), pH units, percent, and Standard Units (SU). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: mg/L|ug/L|ng/L|ppm|ppb|ppt|NTU|CFU/100mL|MPN/100mL|pH_units|percent|SU — 12 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: corrective_action_required
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether corrective action is required based on QC sample failure. True if the QC failure necessitates re-analysis, method adjustment, or other corrective measures; false otherwise.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - Corrective action procedures; EPA QA/QC Guidelines

attributes.name: corrective_action_taken
attributes.description: Description of corrective action taken in response to QC sample failure. May include re-analysis, instrument recalibration, method modification, or sample re-collection. Required for laboratory accreditation and audit trail.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - Corrective action documentation; State laboratory certification requirements

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this QC sample record was first created in the data warehouse. Part of the audit trail for data lineage and compliance.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - Record keeping and traceability; GASB financial reporting standards

attributes.name: detection_limit
attributes.description: Method Detection Limit (MDL) for the analyte and test method at the time of analysis. Represents the minimum concentration that can be measured and reported with 99% confidence that the analyte is greater than zero.
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 136 Appendix B - Definition and Procedure for the Determination of the Method Detection Limit

attributes.name: dilution_factor
attributes.description: Dilution factor applied to the QC sample during preparation or analysis. A value of 1.0 indicates no dilution; values greater than 1.0 indicate the sample was diluted. Used to back-calculate original concentrations.
attributes.references: EPA Method 200.7; Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: expected_concentration
attributes.description: The known or target concentration value for the QC sample. For LCS and CRM, this is the certified value; for matrix spikes, this is the spiked amount plus the native sample concentration; for blanks, this is typically zero.
attributes.references: EPA QA/QC protocols; NIST Standard Reference Materials

attributes.name: lims_sample_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Sample Number
attributes.description: Unique sample identifier assigned by the Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS), such as LabWare. Used for integration and cross-referencing between the data warehouse and the operational LIMS system.
attributes.references: LabWare LIMS data model; ISO/IEC 17025 - Sample identification and traceability

tag_set.value: Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) Sample Number

attributes.name: lower_acceptance_limit
attributes.description: Lower bound of the acceptable range for percent recovery or Relative Percent Difference (RPD). Defined by the analytical method, laboratory Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), or regulatory requirement. QC samples below this limit fail acceptance criteria.
attributes.references: EPA Method-specific QC acceptance criteria; ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: measured_concentration
attributes.description: The actual concentration value obtained from laboratory analysis of the QC sample. Used to calculate recovery and evaluate method performance.
attributes.references: EPA Method 200.7; Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this QC sample record was last modified in the data warehouse. Tracks data lineage and supports audit trail requirements.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - Record keeping and traceability; GASB financial reporting standards

attributes.name: native_concentration
attributes.description: Original concentration of the analyte in the sample before spiking, applicable to matrix spike and matrix spike duplicate QC types. Used in recovery calculations: recovery = (measured - native) / spike * 100.
attributes.references: EPA QA/QC Guidelines; Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: percent_recovery
attributes.description: Calculated percent recovery of the QC sample, computed as (measured_concentration / expected_concentration) * 100. Indicates the accuracy of the analytical method. Typically evaluated against acceptance limits defined in the method or laboratory QA plan.

attributes.name: proficiency_test_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this QC sample is part of an external proficiency testing program (e.g., EPA Water Pollution Performance Evaluation Studies, AWWA proficiency testing). True if part of proficiency testing; false for routine internal QC.
attributes.references: EPA National Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (NELAP); ISO/IEC 17025 - Proficiency testing requirements

attributes.name: proficiency_test_provider
attributes.description: Name of the external proficiency testing provider if this QC sample is part of a proficiency test (e.g., EPA, AWWA, Environmental Resource Associates). Null for routine internal QC samples.
attributes.references: EPA National Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (NELAP); ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: qc_comments
attributes.description: Free-text comments from the analyst or quality assurance officer regarding the QC sample. May include notes on anomalies, corrective actions taken, reasons for failure, or special handling procedures.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - Documentation of deviations and corrective actions

attributes.name: qc_sample_type
attributes.description: Type of quality control sample. Method blank verifies absence of contamination; Laboratory Control Sample (LCS) verifies method accuracy; Matrix Spike (MS) and Matrix Spike Duplicate (MSD) verify matrix interference and precision; field duplicate and field blank verify field collection procedures; surrogate spike verifies extraction efficiency; Certified Reference Material (CRM) verifies instrument calibration. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: method_blank|laboratory_control_sample|matrix_spike|matrix_spike_duplicate|field_duplicate|field_blank|surrogate_spike|certified_reference_material — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
attributes.references: EPA Quality Assurance/Quality Control (QA/QC) Guidelines; ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: qc_status
attributes.description: Pass/fail status of the QC sample based on comparison of percent recovery or Relative Percent Difference (RPD) against acceptance limits. Pass indicates the QC sample met all acceptance criteria; fail indicates one or more criteria were not met; warning indicates results are marginal; pending_review indicates awaiting quality assurance officer review; not_applicable for QC types without numeric acceptance criteria.
attributes.references: EPA QA/QC Guidelines; ISO/IEC 17025 - Data validation requirements

attributes.name: relative_percent_difference
attributes.description: Relative Percent Difference between duplicate QC samples (e.g., matrix spike and matrix spike duplicate, or field duplicates). Calculated as absolute difference divided by the mean, multiplied by 100. Measures precision and reproducibility of the analytical method.
attributes.references: EPA QA/QC Guidelines; Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: reporting_limit
attributes.description: Reporting Limit (RL) or Practical Quantitation Limit (PQL) for the analyte and test method. The minimum concentration that can be reliably quantified and reported to regulatory agencies. Typically 3-5 times the Method Detection Limit (MDL).
attributes.references: EPA 40 CFR Part 136; Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) reporting requirements

attributes.name: review_date
attributes.description: Date the QC sample results were reviewed and validated by the quality assurance officer. Part of the data validation and approval workflow.
attributes.references: ISO/IEC 17025 - Data validation and approval procedures

attributes.name: spike_concentration
attributes.description: Concentration of analyte added to the sample for matrix spike, matrix spike duplicate, or surrogate spike QC types. Null for other QC types. Used to calculate percent recovery in the presence of sample matrix.
attributes.references: EPA QA/QC Guidelines; Standard Methods for the Examination of Water and Wastewater

attributes.name: upper_acceptance_limit
attributes.description: Upper bound of the acceptable range for percent recovery or Relative Percent Difference (RPD). Defined by the analytical method, laboratory Standard Operating Procedure (SOP), or regulatory requirement. QC samples above this limit fail acceptance criteria.
attributes.references: EPA Method-specific QC acceptance criteria; ISO/IEC 17025

attributes.name: secondary_certified_employee_id

attributes.name: source_primary_certified_employee_id

attributes.name: analyst_first_name
attributes.description: First name of the certified laboratory analyst. Used for identification on laboratory reports and chain of custody documentation.

attributes.name: analyst_last_name
attributes.description: Last name of the certified laboratory analyst. Used for identification on laboratory reports and chain of custody documentation.

attributes.name: analyst_middle_initial
attributes.description: Middle initial of the certified laboratory analyst. Optional field for complete name identification.

attributes.name: background_check_date
attributes.description: Date of the most recent background check or security clearance verification. Required for analysts working with sensitive data or in facilities subject to security regulations.

attributes.name: certification_level
attributes.description: Hierarchical level or grade of the certification indicating the complexity of analytical work the analyst is authorized to perform. Higher levels typically authorize more complex testing methods and supervisory responsibilities.

attributes.name: certification_number

attributes.name: certification_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the certification. Active certifications authorize the analyst to perform regulated work; expired, suspended, or revoked certifications prohibit such work until reinstated.
