attributes.description: Free-text field for additional notes, comments, or special instructions related to grant administration, compliance, or coordination.

attributes.name: pass_through_entity_identifying_number
attributes.description: Identifying number assigned by the pass-through entity to this subaward. Required for Single Audit reporting when applicable.

attributes.name: pass_through_entity_name
attributes.description: Name of the pass-through entity if the grant is received from a state or local agency that is itself a federal grant recipient (e.g., 'State Water Resources Control Board'). Null if received directly from federal agency.

attributes.name: period_of_performance_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the grant period. All allowable costs must be incurred by this date. Extensions require formal amendment.

attributes.name: period_of_performance_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the grant period during which costs may be incurred and charged to the grant. May differ from award_date.

attributes.name: program_name
attributes.description: Name of the specific grant program under which the award was made (e.g., 'Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act (WIFIA)', 'Clean Water State Revolving Fund (CWSRF)', 'Drinking Water State Revolving Fund (DWSRF)', 'American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA) Infrastructure Grants').

attributes.name: project_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the capital or operational project funded by this grant (e.g., 'Replacement of 5 miles of aging water distribution mains in the downtown district', 'Upgrade of wastewater treatment plant secondary clarifiers and UV disinfection system').

attributes.name: project_location
attributes.description: Geographic location or service area where the grant-funded project is being implemented (e.g., 'Downtown Water Treatment Plant, 123 Main St', 'District 4 Distribution Network').

attributes.name: remaining_balance
attributes.description: Dollar amount of grant funds still available for drawdown. Calculated as award_amount minus total_amount_drawn.
attributes.references: GASB Statement No. 33 - Accounting and Financial Reporting for Nonexchange Transactions

attributes.name: repayment_term_months
attributes.description: Total repayment period in months for loan-type grants. Null for non-repayable grants.
attributes.references: GASB Statement No. 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: reporting_frequency
attributes.description: Frequency at which financial and performance reports must be submitted to the grantor agency (monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, annually, or as required by specific milestones).

attributes.name: single_audit_required_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this grant is subject to Single Audit Act requirements (OMB Uniform Guidance). True if the utility expends $750,000 or more in federal awards in a fiscal year.
attributes.references: Single Audit Act (2 CFR 200 Subpart F)

attributes.name: total_amount_drawn
attributes.description: Cumulative dollar amount of grant funds that have been drawn down or reimbursed to date. Updated as drawdown requests are processed.
attributes.references: GASB Statement No. 33 - Accounting and Financial Reporting for Nonexchange Transactions

products.name: grant_expenditure
products.description: Grant expenditure transaction recording costs charged against specific grants for reimbursement and compliance tracking. Captures grant ID, expenditure date, cost category, vendor or payroll reference, amount, eligible/ineligible classification, drawdown request reference, and federal/state reporting period. Supports grant drawdown requests, single audit Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (SEFA), and grantor reporting.
products.reference: SEFA / OMB Uniform Guidance / GASB Grant Expenditure

attributes.name: grant_expenditure_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the grant expenditure transaction record.

attributes.name: cip_project_id
attributes.description: Reference to the capital or operational project to which this expenditure is assigned.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Grant expenditures are allocated to cost centers. The cost_center_code STRING should be replaced with FK to cost_center.cost_center_id.

attributes.name: drawdown_request_id
attributes.description: Reference to the grant drawdown or reimbursement request in which this expenditure was included.

attributes.name: employee_id
attributes.description: Reference to the employee for payroll-related expenditures charged to the grant.

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Grant expenditures post to GL accounts. The gl_account_code STRING should be replaced with FK to general_ledger.general_ledger_id.

attributes.name: grant_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific grant against which this expenditure is charged.

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Reference to the vendor or supplier from whom goods or services were purchased, if applicable.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.work_order. Business justification: Grant-funded infrastructure projects track expenditures to specific work orders for federal/state compliance reporting, single audit requirements, and grant reimbursement documentation. Required for D

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date on which the expenditure was approved for grant charging.

attributes.name: approval_status
attributes.description: The current approval status of the expenditure for grant charging purposes.

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the individual who approved this expenditure for grant charging.

attributes.name: audit_finding_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this expenditure has been flagged in a grant audit or single audit finding.

attributes.name: audit_finding_reference
attributes.description: Reference number or description of the audit finding associated with this expenditure, if applicable.

attributes.name: cfda_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance (CFDA) Number
attributes.description: The CFDA number identifying the federal program under which the grant was awarded (used for SEFA reporting).

tag_set.value: Catalog of Federal Domestic Assistance (CFDA) Number

attributes.name: cost_category
attributes.description: The classification of the expenditure according to grant budget categories (personnel, fringe benefits, travel, equipment, supplies, contractual, construction, other direct costs, indirect costs). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: personnel|fringe_benefits|travel|equipment|supplies|contractual|construction|other_direct|indirect — 9 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this grant expenditure record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: The three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the expenditure amount (typically USD for U.S. water utilities).

attributes.name: grant_expenditure_description
attributes.description: A detailed narrative description of the goods, services, or activities for which the expenditure was incurred.

attributes.name: eligibility_classification
attributes.description: Classification indicating whether the expenditure is eligible, ineligible, partially eligible, or pending review for grant reimbursement.

attributes.name: eligible_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the expenditure amount that is eligible for reimbursement under the grant terms.

attributes.name: expenditure_amount
attributes.description: The total dollar amount of the expenditure charged to the grant.

attributes.name: expenditure_date
attributes.description: The date on which the expenditure was incurred or the transaction occurred.

attributes.name: federal_award_identification_number
attributes.description: The unique Federal Award Identification Number assigned by the federal agency for tracking and reporting purposes.

attributes.name: ineligible_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the expenditure amount that is not eligible for reimbursement under the grant terms.

attributes.name: invoice_number
attributes.description: The invoice or payment document number associated with this expenditure.

attributes.name: match_amount
attributes.description: The dollar amount of this expenditure that counts toward the grantee match or cost-sharing requirement.

attributes.name: match_requirement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether this expenditure is used to satisfy a grant match or cost-sharing requirement.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this grant expenditure record was last modified or updated.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes or comments regarding the expenditure, eligibility determination, or special circumstances.

attributes.name: posting_date
attributes.description: The date on which the expenditure was posted to the general ledger or financial system.

attributes.name: purchase_order_number
attributes.description: The purchase order number associated with this expenditure, if applicable.

attributes.name: reporting_period_end_date
attributes.description: The end date of the federal or state reporting period to which this expenditure is assigned.

attributes.name: reporting_period_start_date
attributes.description: The start date of the federal or state reporting period to which this expenditure is assigned.

attributes.name: wbs_element
attributes.description: The work breakdown structure element code for detailed project cost tracking within the grant.

products.name: debt_instrument
products.description: Debt portfolio management for the water utility's long-term obligations including revenue bonds, GO bonds, SRF loans, WIFIA loans, and commercial paper. Covers both instrument master data (type, issuance date, maturity, principal, interest rate, bond rating, trustee, GASB classification) and debt service payment transactions (scheduled/actual principal and interest payments, payment source fund, reserve fund draws, trustee confirmations). Supports amortization schedule management, bond covenant compliance monitoring, rate case preparation, and CAFR long-term debt disclosures.
products.reference: GASB Long-Term Debt / MSRB Bond Disclosure

attributes.name: debt_instrument_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the debt instrument record in the water utility's long-term debt portfolio.

attributes.name: cip_project_id
attributes.description: add column cip_project_id (BIGINT) with FK to project.cip_project.cip_project_id - revenue bonds and SRF loans are typically tied to specific capital projects

attributes.name: fund_id
attributes.description: add column fund_id (BIGINT) with FK to finance.fund.fund_id - debt instruments are issued against specific funds in municipal fund accounting

attributes.name: amortization_type
attributes.description: The structure of principal repayment over the life of the debt. Level principal has equal principal payments; level debt service has equal combined principal and interest payments; bullet has single principal payment at maturity; serial has staggered maturities; term has single maturity date.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: bond_counsel_name
attributes.description: The name of the law firm that provided the legal opinion on the validity and tax-exempt status of the debt issuance.
attributes.references: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) Rule G-23

attributes.name: bond_rating
attributes.description: The credit quality rating assigned to the debt instrument by rating agencies (e.g., Moody's, S&P, Fitch). Common ratings include AAA, AA, A, BBB, etc. Higher ratings indicate lower credit risk and typically result in lower interest costs.
attributes.references: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) Rule G-17

attributes.name: cafr_reporting_category
attributes.business_glossary_term: Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) Reporting Category
attributes.description: The category under which this debt instrument is reported in the utility's CAFR. Water utilities typically report under business-type activities as enterprise funds.

tag_set.value: Comprehensive Annual Financial Report (CAFR) Reporting Category

attributes.name: call_date
attributes.description: The earliest date on which the issuer may exercise the call option to redeem the debt instrument before maturity. Null if the instrument is non-callable.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: call_premium_percentage
attributes.description: The premium above par value that the issuer must pay to bondholders if the debt is called before maturity, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 2.0000 represents 2.00% premium). Null if non-callable.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: callable_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the issuer has the right to redeem (call) the debt instrument before its stated maturity date. True indicates callable; False indicates non-callable.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: coupon_frequency
attributes.description: The frequency at which interest payments (coupons) are made to bondholders or lenders. Semi-annual is most common for municipal bonds.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: covenant_description
attributes.description: Description of financial covenants and restrictions imposed by the debt agreement, such as debt service coverage ratio requirements, rate covenant obligations, reserve fund requirements, or restrictions on additional debt issuance.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this debt instrument record was first created in the system.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: cusip_number
attributes.business_glossary_term: Committee on Uniform Securities Identification Procedures (CUSIP) Number
attributes.description: The 9-character alphanumeric identifier assigned to the debt instrument for trading and settlement purposes in the securities market. Format: 3 digits (issuer), 6 alphanumeric (issue), 1 check digit.
attributes.references: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) Rule G-34

tag_set.value: Committee on Uniform Securities Identification Procedures (CUSIP) Number

attributes.name: debt_service_reserve_requirement
attributes.description: The required balance to be maintained in the debt service reserve fund as specified in the bond indenture, typically equal to maximum annual debt service or a percentage of outstanding principal.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: gasb_classification
attributes.description: The classification of the debt instrument for GASB financial reporting purposes. Long-term debt has maturity beyond one year; short-term debt matures within one year; current portion represents principal due within the next fiscal year; non-current portion represents principal due beyond the next fiscal year.

attributes.name: instrument_number
attributes.description: The externally-known unique identifier or serial number assigned to the debt instrument by the issuer, trustee, or financial institution (e.g., bond CUSIP, loan agreement number).
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: instrument_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the debt instrument. Active indicates the debt is outstanding and serviced; matured indicates principal fully repaid at term end; defeased indicates legally satisfied through irrevocable trust; refunded indicates replaced by new debt issuance; defaulted indicates payment obligations not met; cancelled indicates instrument voided before issuance.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 7 - Advance Refundings Resulting in Defeasance of Debt

attributes.name: instrument_type
attributes.description: Classification of the debt instrument by its legal and financial structure. Revenue bonds are secured by utility revenues; general obligation bonds by taxing authority; SRF (State Revolving Fund) loans provide low-cost financing for water infrastructure; WIFIA (Water Infrastructure Finance and Innovation Act) loans offer federal credit assistance; commercial paper provides short-term financing; bank loans are direct borrowings from financial institutions.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 34 - Basic Financial Statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis for State and Local Governments

attributes.name: insurance_provider
attributes.description: The name of the bond insurance company providing credit enhancement for the debt instrument, if applicable. Bond insurance guarantees timely payment of principal and interest in case of issuer default.
attributes.references: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) Rule G-17

attributes.name: interest_calculation_method
attributes.description: The day-count convention used to calculate accrued interest. 30/360 assumes 30-day months and 360-day years; Actual/360 uses actual days and 360-day years; Actual/365 uses actual days and 365-day years; Actual/Actual uses actual days and actual year length.
attributes.references: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) Rule G-33

attributes.name: interest_rate
attributes.description: The annual interest rate applied to the outstanding principal balance, expressed as a percentage (e.g., 3.5000 represents 3.50%). For variable rate instruments, this represents the current rate.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: interest_rate_type
attributes.description: Classification of the interest rate structure. Fixed rates remain constant over the life of the instrument; variable rates adjust periodically based on market indices; zero coupon instruments accrue interest but pay at maturity.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 53 - Accounting and Financial Reporting for Derivative Instruments

attributes.name: isin_number
attributes.description: The 12-character alphanumeric code that uniquely identifies the debt instrument in international securities markets. Format: 2-letter country code + 9-character national identifier + 1 check digit.

attributes.name: issuance_date
attributes.description: The date on which the debt instrument was originally issued and funds were received by the water utility.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: liquidity_provider_name
attributes.description: For variable rate demand obligations, the name of the financial institution providing the standby bond purchase agreement or letter of credit to ensure liquidity if bonds cannot be remarketed.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: maturity_date
attributes.description: The date on which the final principal payment is due and the debt instrument obligation is fully satisfied.

attributes.name: modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The timestamp when this debt instrument record was last modified or updated in the system.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: original_principal_amount
attributes.description: The total face value or principal amount of the debt instrument at issuance, before any payments or amortization.

attributes.name: outstanding_principal_balance
attributes.description: The current unpaid principal balance remaining on the debt instrument after all principal payments to date.

attributes.name: paying_agent_name
attributes.description: The name of the financial institution designated to distribute principal and interest payments to bondholders on behalf of the issuer.
attributes.references: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) Rule G-34

attributes.name: project_description
attributes.description: Detailed description of the specific capital projects or initiatives funded by this debt instrument, including water treatment plant upgrades, distribution network expansion, wastewater treatment improvements, or other infrastructure investments.

attributes.name: purpose
attributes.description: The intended use of proceeds from the debt issuance, such as capital improvement projects (CIP), infrastructure replacement, system expansion, refunding existing debt, or working capital needs.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 34 - Management's Discussion and Analysis

attributes.name: rate_case_inclusion_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether debt service costs for this instrument are included in the utility's rate base for rate-setting purposes. True indicates included in rates; False indicates excluded.

attributes.name: rate_reset_frequency
attributes.description: For variable rate debt, the frequency at which the interest rate is recalculated and adjusted based on the underlying index.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 53 - Accounting and Financial Reporting for Derivative Instruments

attributes.name: rating_agency
attributes.description: The name of the credit rating agency that assigned the bond rating (e.g., Moody's Investors Service, Standard & Poor's, Fitch Ratings).
attributes.references: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) Rule G-17

attributes.name: remarketing_agent_name
attributes.description: For variable rate demand obligations, the name of the financial institution responsible for resetting the interest rate and remarketing bonds tendered by investors.
attributes.references: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) Rule G-17

attributes.name: security_type
attributes.description: The type of security or collateral backing the debt instrument. Revenue pledge is secured by utility operating revenues; general obligation by taxing power; special assessment by property assessments; moral obligation by non-binding commitment; unsecured has no specific collateral.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 34 - Notes to Financial Statements

attributes.name: tax_exempt_flag
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether interest income from this debt instrument is exempt from federal income tax. True indicates tax-exempt; False indicates taxable. Most municipal water utility bonds are tax-exempt.
attributes.references: Internal Revenue Code Section 103 - Interest on State and Local Bonds

attributes.name: trustee_name
attributes.description: The name of the financial institution serving as trustee, responsible for safeguarding bondholders' interests, holding collateral, and ensuring compliance with bond covenants.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: underwriter_name
attributes.description: The name of the investment banking firm or financial institution that underwrote the debt issuance and facilitated its sale to investors.
attributes.references: Municipal Securities Rulemaking Board (MSRB) Rule G-17

attributes.name: variable_rate_index
attributes.description: For variable rate debt, the market index to which the interest rate is tied, such as SOFR (Secured Overnight Financing Rate), LIBOR (being phased out), SIFMA (Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association Municipal Swap Index), or Prime Rate.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 53 - Accounting and Financial Reporting for Derivative Instruments

products.name: debt_service_payment
products.description: Debt service payment transaction recording scheduled and actual principal and interest payments on the water utility's debt obligations. Captures debt instrument reference, payment due date, actual payment date, principal amount, interest amount, total payment, payment source fund, reserve fund draw indicator, and trustee confirmation number. Supports GASB debt service fund accounting and bond covenant compliance monitoring.
products.reference: GASB Debt Service / Bond Indenture Payment Schedule

attributes.name: debt_service_payment_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the debt service payment transaction.

attributes.name: bank_account_id
attributes.description: add column bank_account_id (BIGINT) with FK to finance.bank_account.bank_account_id - debt service payments are disbursed from specific bank accounts

attributes.name: cip_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.cip_project. Business justification: Debt service payments for project-specific bonds must be tracked to the funded project for rate case cost recovery and debt service coverage ratio calculations.

attributes.name: debt_instrument_id
attributes.description: Reference to the specific debt instrument (bond, loan, note) for which this payment is made.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: fund_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fund. Business justification: Debt service payments are drawn from specific funds. The payment_source_fund_code STRING should be replaced with FK to fund.fund_id.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date on which the debt service payment was approved for processing by authorized personnel.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: Name or identifier of the authorized person who approved the debt service payment for processing.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: covenant_compliance_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this debt service payment was made in compliance with all bond covenants and debt service coverage requirements.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the debt service payment record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the debt service payment. Typically USD for U.S. water utilities.

attributes.name: days_late
attributes.description: Number of days the debt service payment was made after the due date, if applicable.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: debt_service_coverage_ratio
attributes.description: The debt service coverage ratio calculated at the time of this payment, representing the ratio of net revenues available for debt service to the debt service payment amount, used for bond covenant monitoring.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: due_date
attributes.description: The scheduled date on which the debt service payment is contractually due per the bond indenture or loan agreement.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: fees_amount
attributes.description: Additional fees associated with the debt service payment, including trustee fees, paying agent fees, or administrative charges.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: fiscal_period
attributes.description: The fiscal period (month) within the fiscal year in which the debt service payment is recorded.

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year in which the debt service payment is recorded for financial reporting and budgeting purposes.

attributes.name: gl_document_number
attributes.description: The general ledger document or journal entry number associated with the debt service payment transaction in SAP FI or Tyler Munis.

attributes.name: gl_posting_date
attributes.description: The date on which the debt service payment transaction was posted to the general ledger in the ERP system.

attributes.name: interest_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the debt service payment applied to interest expense on the debt instrument.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the debt service payment record was last modified or updated in the system.

attributes.name: late_payment_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the debt service payment was made after the contractual due date.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: late_payment_penalty_amount
attributes.description: Penalty amount assessed for late payment of debt service, if applicable per the bond indenture or loan agreement.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes or comments regarding the debt service payment, including any special circumstances, adjustments, or explanations.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: payment_date
attributes.description: The actual date on which the debt service payment was made or processed by the utility.

attributes.name: payment_method
attributes.description: The method by which the debt service payment was transmitted to the trustee or paying agent.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: payment_number
attributes.description: Business identifier for the debt service payment, typically sequential or following a numbering convention established by the utility or trustee.

attributes.name: payment_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the debt service payment indicating whether it is scheduled, processed, confirmed by trustee, failed, or reversed.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: payment_type
attributes.description: Classification of the debt service payment indicating whether it is a scheduled payment, prepayment, defeasance, refunding, or penalty payment.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 23 - Accounting and Financial Reporting for Refundings of Debt

attributes.name: premium_discount_amortization
attributes.description: The amortization amount for bond premium or discount allocated to this payment period, following the effective interest method or straight-line method as applicable.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: principal_amount
attributes.description: The portion of the debt service payment applied to the principal balance of the debt instrument.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: reserve_fund_draw_amount
attributes.description: The amount drawn from the debt service reserve fund to supplement this payment, if applicable.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: reserve_fund_draw_indicator
attributes.description: Boolean flag indicating whether this debt service payment required a draw from the debt service reserve fund to meet the obligation.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: sap_company_code
attributes.description: SAP ERP company code associated with the debt service payment transaction for multi-entity utilities.
attributes.references: SAP FI/CO - Financial Accounting and Controlling

attributes.name: total_payment_amount
attributes.description: The total amount of the debt service payment, including principal, interest, amortization, and fees.

attributes.name: transaction_reference_number
attributes.description: Bank or financial system transaction reference number for the debt service payment, used for reconciliation and audit trail.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: trustee_confirmation_number
attributes.description: Confirmation or reference number provided by the bond trustee or paying agent acknowledging receipt and processing of the debt service payment.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: trustee_name
attributes.description: Name of the bond trustee or paying agent responsible for receiving and disbursing the debt service payment to bondholders.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: tyler_munis_transaction_reference
attributes.description: Tyler Technologies Munis system transaction identifier for the debt service payment, used for municipal utilities.

products.name: finance_rate_case
products.description: Rate case master record for formal water and wastewater rate proceedings filed with the Public Utilities Commission or approved by the utility board. Captures rate case type (general rate case, interim rate, surcharge), filing date, test year, requested revenue requirement, approved revenue requirement, rate effective date, rate case consultant, regulatory docket number, and rate design methodology. Central to utility financial planning and regulatory compliance.
products.reference: PUC Rate Case / AWWA Rate Design Manual

attributes.name: finance_rate_case_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the rate case proceeding. Primary key for the rate case master record.

attributes.name: territory_id
attributes.description: add column territory_id (BIGINT) with FK to service.territory.territory_id - rate cases are filed for specific service territories/jurisdictions

attributes.name: allowed_rate_of_return
attributes.description: The overall rate of return on rate base authorized by the regulatory commission, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0725 for 7.25%). Represents the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) including debt and equity components.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate of Return Standards

attributes.name: allowed_return_on_equity
attributes.description: The authorized return on equity component of the rate of return, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0950 for 9.50%). Represents the profit margin allowed on shareholder equity investment in the utility.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate of Return Standards

attributes.name: appeal_filed_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether any party filed an appeal or request for rehearing of the commission decision. Appeals may delay rate implementation or require refund provisions.

attributes.name: approved_revenue_requirement
attributes.description: Total annual revenue requirement approved by the regulatory commission or utility board. This is the final authorized revenue level after regulatory review, hearings, and adjustments. May differ from the requested amount due to disallowed costs, rate base adjustments, or modified return on equity. Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate Case Decision Standards

attributes.name: capital_improvement_program_amount
attributes.description: Total value of the Capital Improvement Program (CIP) or Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) plan supporting the rate case, covering planned infrastructure investments during the test year and rate period. Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: American Water Works Association (AWWA) Asset Management Standards

attributes.name: case_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the rate case proceeding. Tracks progression from initial draft through regulatory review, hearings, commission decision, and final disposition. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: draft|filed|pending_review|hearing_scheduled|decision_pending|approved|denied|withdrawn — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

attributes.name: case_type
attributes.description: Classification of the rate case proceeding. General rate case (GRC) is a comprehensive review of revenue requirements; interim adjustments address specific cost changes; surcharges recover specific program costs; cost of service reviews cost allocation; rate design modifies rate structure without changing revenue; emergency rates address urgent financial needs.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate Case Classification Standards

attributes.name: commercial_rate_impact_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage change in typical commercial customer bills resulting from the approved rate case.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate Impact Reporting Standards

attributes.name: consultant
attributes.description: Name of the external consulting firm or advisor retained to prepare the rate case filing, cost of service study, and regulatory testimony. Common firms include Black & Veatch, Raftelis, NewGen Strategies, and specialized rate consultants.
attributes.references: Internal Procurement and Vendor Management Standards

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this rate case record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

attributes.name: customer_class_allocation_method
attributes.description: The cost allocation methodology used to distribute revenue requirements across customer classes (residential, commercial, industrial, public authority). Base-extra-capacity allocates fixed costs by capacity and variable by usage; commodity-demand splits by consumption and peak demand; customer count uses simple per-account allocation; meter equivalent weights by meter size; peak demand allocates by maximum usage contribution.
attributes.references: American Water Works Association (AWWA) M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: debt_service_amount
attributes.description: Annual debt service costs (principal and interest payments) on utility bonds and loans included in the revenue requirement. Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB)

attributes.name: decision_date
attributes.description: Date the regulatory commission issued its final decision and order on the rate case. This date establishes the official record and triggers appeal deadlines.

attributes.name: decision_document_url
attributes.description: Web link to the official commission decision document, order, or ruling. Typically hosted on the Public Utilities Commission website or document management system.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Electronic Filing Standards

attributes.name: depreciation_expense_amount
attributes.description: Annual depreciation expense included in the revenue requirement, calculated based on approved depreciation rates and asset lives for utility plant and equipment. Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB)

attributes.name: docket_number
attributes.description: Official docket or case number assigned by the Public Utilities Commission (PUC) or regulatory body for tracking the rate proceeding. This is the externally-known identifier used in all regulatory filings and correspondence.

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: Date the rate case application was formally filed with the Public Utilities Commission or regulatory authority. This date triggers statutory review timelines and procedural deadlines.

attributes.name: gasb_compliance_notes
attributes.business_glossary_term: Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) Compliance Notes
attributes.description: Free-text notes documenting compliance with Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) requirements for municipal utilities, including fund accounting, regulatory asset/liability treatment, and financial statement presentation.

tag_set.value: Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB) Compliance Notes

attributes.name: hearing_date
attributes.description: Date of the formal public hearing before the regulatory commission where testimony is presented, witnesses are cross-examined, and public comment is received.

attributes.name: industrial_rate_impact_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage change in typical industrial customer bills resulting from the approved rate case.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate Impact Reporting Standards

attributes.name: intervenor_count
attributes.description: Number of parties granted intervenor status in the rate case proceeding. Intervenors may include consumer advocates, industrial customer groups, environmental organizations, or other stakeholders with standing to participate.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when this rate case record was last updated. Used for audit trail and change tracking.

attributes.name: lead_attorney
attributes.description: Name of the lead legal counsel representing the utility in the rate case proceeding. May be in-house counsel or external regulatory law firm.

attributes.name: next_rate_case_anticipated_date
attributes.description: Anticipated filing date for the next general rate case. Used for financial planning and analysis (FP&A) and long-term capital planning. May be driven by regulatory requirements, financial need, or strategic timing.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional context, special circumstances, regulatory conditions, or internal commentary related to the rate case proceeding.

attributes.name: operating_expense_amount
attributes.description: Total annual operating expenses included in the approved revenue requirement. Includes operations and maintenance (O&M) costs, administrative expenses, purchased water, power, chemicals, labor, and other recurring costs. Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB)

attributes.name: public_notice_date
attributes.description: Date public notice of the rate case filing was published in newspapers, utility bills, or other media as required by regulatory rules. Triggers public comment period.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Public Notice Requirements

attributes.name: rate_base_amount
attributes.description: The net value of utility plant and equipment upon which the utility is allowed to earn a return. Calculated as gross plant in service plus working capital minus accumulated depreciation and contributions in aid of construction. Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB)

attributes.name: rate_design_methodology
attributes.description: The pricing methodology used to allocate the approved revenue requirement across customer classes and rate components. Cost of service allocates based on cost causation; value of service considers customer willingness to pay; marginal cost reflects incremental supply costs; tiered conservation encourages efficiency; uniform rate applies flat pricing; lifeline protects low-income customers.
attributes.references: American Water Works Association (AWWA) M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: rate_effective_date
attributes.description: Date on which the approved rates become effective and are applied to customer bills. May be subject to refund provisions during appeal periods or interim rate periods.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate Implementation Standards

attributes.name: regulatory_lag_days
attributes.description: Number of days between rate case filing and rate effective date. Regulatory lag represents the period during which the utility operates under outdated rates while awaiting approval, potentially impacting financial performance.

attributes.name: requested_revenue_requirement
attributes.description: Total annual revenue requirement requested by the utility in the rate case filing. Represents the utility's calculation of the revenue needed to cover operating expenses (OPEX), capital costs (CAPEX), debt service, and allowed return on investment (ROI). Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB)

attributes.name: residential_rate_impact_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage change in typical residential customer bills resulting from the approved rate case. Used for public communication and affordability analysis.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate Impact Reporting Standards

attributes.name: revenue_increase_amount
attributes.description: Dollar amount of the approved revenue increase (or decrease if negative) compared to current authorized revenue levels. Calculated as approved revenue requirement minus current revenue requirement. Expressed in USD.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate Case Decision Standards

attributes.name: revenue_increase_percentage
attributes.description: Percentage increase (or decrease if negative) in authorized revenue compared to current levels. Calculated as (revenue increase amount / current revenue requirement) * 100. Used for public communication and rate impact analysis.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate Case Decision Standards

attributes.name: settlement_agreement_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the rate case was resolved through a negotiated settlement agreement among parties rather than a fully litigated commission decision. Settlements often result in faster resolution and reduced regulatory costs.

attributes.name: test_year_end_date
attributes.description: Ending date of the test year period used to establish the utility's revenue requirements and cost structure.
attributes.references: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB)

attributes.name: test_year_start_date
attributes.description: Beginning date of the test year period used to establish the utility's revenue requirements and cost structure. The test year is the 12-month period (historical or forecasted) upon which rate calculations are based.
attributes.references: Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), Governmental Accounting Standards Board (GASB)

attributes.name: test_year_type
attributes.description: Indicates whether the test year is based on historical actual data, forecasted future data, or a hybrid approach combining historical base with known adjustments. Regulatory bodies may have preferences or requirements for test year methodology.
attributes.references: Public Utilities Commission Rate Case Standards

products.name: revenue_requirement
products.description: Revenue requirement calculation record supporting rate case preparation and annual budget reconciliation. Captures test year, cost of service components (O&M expenses, depreciation, debt service, return on rate base, taxes), allocated by customer class (residential, commercial, industrial, municipal), revenue sufficiency gap, and rate adjustment percentage. Supports PUC filings and AWWA cost-of-service methodology.
products.reference: AWWA M1 Manual / PUC Revenue Requirement

attributes.name: revenue_requirement_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the revenue requirement calculation record.

attributes.name: billing_rate_schedule_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to billing.rate_schedule. Business justification: Revenue requirements drive rate schedule design in rate cases. Rate analysts and regulators need to trace which rate schedules implement each revenue requirement calculation for cost-of-service valida

attributes.name: cip_project_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to project.cip_project. Business justification: Revenue requirements include specific CIP project costs for rate base calculations, depreciation expense, and return on investment. Essential for rate case filings.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Revenue requirements are allocated to cost centers. The cost_center_code STRING should be replaced with FK to cost_center.cost_center_id.

attributes.name: finance_rate_case_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.rate_case. Business justification: Revenue requirements support rate cases. The docket_number STRING should be replaced with FK to rate_case.finance_rate_case_id (note: rate_case PK is finance_rate_case_id, not rate_case_id).

attributes.name: fund_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fund. Business justification: Revenue requirements are calculated by fund. The fund_code STRING should be replaced with FK to fund.fund_id.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: The date when the revenue requirement calculation was approved by the regulatory authority or Public Utilities Commission (PUC).
attributes.references: State Public Utilities Commission Rate Case Filing Requirements

attributes.name: approved_by
attributes.description: The name or identifier of the regulatory commissioner or authority representative who approved the revenue requirement.

attributes.name: authorized_rate_of_return_percentage
attributes.description: The rate of return on rate base authorized by the Public Utilities Commission (PUC), typically based on the utility's weighted average cost of capital (WACC).
attributes.references: State Public Utilities Commission Rate Case Filing Requirements

attributes.name: calculation_method
attributes.description: The methodology used to calculate the revenue requirement, typically cost-of-service for water utilities following AWWA standards.
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: calculation_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the revenue requirement calculation in the regulatory approval process.

attributes.name: capital_expenditure_amount
attributes.description: Planned capital expenditures allocated to this customer class for the test year, supporting infrastructure investment and asset renewal programs.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 34 - Basic Financial Statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis for State and Local Governments

attributes.name: cost_allocation_method
attributes.description: The method used to allocate costs among customer classes, such as base-extra capacity, commodity-demand, customer count, meter equivalent, or consumption ratio.
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this revenue requirement record was first created in the system.

attributes.name: current_revenue_amount
attributes.description: Current annual revenue collected from this customer class under existing rates, used to calculate the revenue sufficiency gap.
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: customer_class
attributes.description: The customer class or rate class for which this revenue requirement component is allocated (residential, commercial, industrial, municipal, wholesale, fire protection).
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: debt_service_amount
attributes.description: Annual debt service obligations (principal and interest payments) allocated to this customer class for outstanding bonds and loans financing capital improvements.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: depreciation_expense_amount
attributes.description: Annual depreciation expense allocated to this customer class based on the utility's asset base and approved depreciation schedules.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 34 - Basic Financial Statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis for State and Local Governments

attributes.name: effective_date
attributes.description: The date when the approved revenue requirement and associated rate adjustments become effective for customer billing.
attributes.references: State Public Utilities Commission Rate Case Filing Requirements

attributes.name: filing_date
attributes.description: The date when the revenue requirement calculation was filed with the Public Utilities Commission (PUC) or regulatory authority for rate case proceedings.
attributes.references: State Public Utilities Commission Rate Case Filing Requirements

attributes.name: grant_funding_amount
attributes.description: Grant funding or subsidies allocated to this customer class that offset the revenue requirement, such as EPA grants or state infrastructure funding.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 33 - Accounting and Financial Reporting for Nonexchange Transactions

attributes.name: last_modified_by
attributes.description: The user ID or name of the person who last modified this revenue requirement record.

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: The date and time when this revenue requirement record was last modified.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Additional notes, comments, or explanations regarding the revenue requirement calculation, assumptions, or regulatory adjustments.

attributes.name: om_expense_amount
attributes.description: Total operations and maintenance expenses allocated to this customer class for the test year, including labor, chemicals, utilities, and routine maintenance costs.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 34 - Basic Financial Statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis for State and Local Governments

attributes.name: operating_expenditure_amount
attributes.description: Total operating expenditures allocated to this customer class for the test year, including O&M expenses and administrative costs.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 34 - Basic Financial Statements and Management's Discussion and Analysis for State and Local Governments

attributes.name: rate_adjustment_percentage
attributes.description: The percentage rate increase or decrease required for this customer class to meet the revenue requirement, calculated as (revenue sufficiency gap / current revenue) * 100.
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: rate_base_amount
attributes.description: The net plant investment (original cost of utility plant in service less accumulated depreciation) allocated to this customer class, used to calculate the return on rate base.
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: regulatory_authority
attributes.description: The name of the regulatory authority or Public Utilities Commission (PUC) that has jurisdiction over this revenue requirement filing.
attributes.references: State Public Utilities Commission Rate Case Filing Requirements

attributes.name: return_on_rate_base_amount
attributes.description: The allowed return on the utility's rate base (net plant investment) allocated to this customer class, calculated as rate base multiplied by the authorized rate of return.
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: revenue_sufficiency_gap_amount
attributes.description: The difference between the total revenue requirement and current revenue, representing the additional revenue needed from this customer class. Positive values indicate a revenue shortfall; negative values indicate a surplus.
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: tax_expense_amount
attributes.description: Income taxes, property taxes, and other tax obligations allocated to this customer class for the test year.
attributes.references: GASB Statement 62 - Codification of Accounting and Financial Reporting Guidance

attributes.name: test_year
attributes.description: The fiscal year used as the basis for the revenue requirement calculation, typically the historical year or projected year for rate case analysis.
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: total_revenue_requirement_amount
attributes.description: Total revenue requirement for this customer class, calculated as the sum of O&M expenses, depreciation, debt service, return on rate base, and taxes.
attributes.references: AWWA M1 Manual - Principles of Water Rates, Fees, and Charges

attributes.name: created_by
attributes.description: The user ID or name of the person who created this revenue requirement record.

products.name: encumbrance
products.description: Budgetary encumbrance record reserving appropriated funds for committed obligations not yet expended, including purchase orders, contracts, and blanket agreements. Captures encumbrance type (pre-encumbrance, encumbrance), originating document reference, fund, cost center, GL account, original amount, liquidated amount, outstanding balance, fiscal year, and period. Essential for governmental budgetary control — prevents over-expenditure of appropriated funds and supports available balance reporting per GASB standards.
products.reference: GASB Encumbrance Accounting / Tyler Munis Encumbrance

attributes.name: encumbrance_id
attributes.description: Unique identifier for the encumbrance record. Primary key.
attributes.references: GASB 54 - Fund Balance Reporting and Governmental Fund Type Definitions

attributes.name: cip_project_id
attributes.description: Capital Improvement Program (CIP) project identifier or work breakdown structure (WBS) element if the encumbrance is associated with a capital project.

attributes.name: cost_center_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Encumbrances are allocated to cost centers. The cost_center_code STRING should be replaced with FK to cost_center.cost_center_id.

attributes.name: fund_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.fund. Business justification: Encumbrances reserve funds. The fund_code STRING should be replaced with FK to fund.fund_id.

attributes.name: general_ledger_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to finance.general_ledger. Business justification: Encumbrances post to GL accounts. The gl_account_code STRING should be replaced with FK to general_ledger.general_ledger_id.

attributes.name: grant_id
attributes.description: Grant identifier if the encumbrance is funded by a federal, state, or local grant program, enabling grant expenditure tracking and compliance reporting.
attributes.references: 2 CFR 200 - Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards

attributes.name: vendor_id
attributes.description: Identifier of the vendor or contractor to whom the encumbrance obligation is owed, linking to the supplier master data.

attributes.name: work_order_id
attributes.description: Foreign key linking to asset.work_order. Business justification: Purchase requisitions for work order materials create budget encumbrances before invoicing. Essential for commitment accounting, budget control, and preventing cost overruns on maintenance and capital

attributes.name: accounting_period
attributes.description: Accounting period within the fiscal year when the encumbrance was recorded (e.g., 01, 02,.., 12 or period name).

attributes.name: amount
attributes.description: Original total amount of budget funds reserved by the encumbrance at the time of commitment, representing the expected obligation.

attributes.name: approval_date
attributes.description: Date the encumbrance was approved by the authorized approver, establishing the commitment as valid.

attributes.name: approver_name
attributes.description: Name of the manager or authorized official who approved the encumbrance, ensuring budgetary control and authorization.

attributes.name: budget_line_item
attributes.description: Specific budget line item or appropriation code against which the encumbrance is charged, enabling detailed budget vs. actual tracking.

attributes.name: business_area
attributes.description: Business area or segment code for internal management reporting, enabling cross-functional analysis (e.g., water treatment, wastewater, distribution).

attributes.name: closed_date
attributes.description: Date the encumbrance was closed, either through full liquidation, cancellation, or fiscal year-end closure process.

attributes.name: company_code
attributes.description: SAP company code or Tyler Munis entity identifier representing the legal entity or organizational unit recording the encumbrance.

attributes.name: contract_end_date
attributes.description: End date of the contract or service agreement associated with the encumbrance, if applicable.

attributes.name: contract_start_date
attributes.description: Start date of the contract or service agreement associated with the encumbrance, if applicable.

attributes.name: created_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the encumbrance record was first created in the lakehouse silver layer.

attributes.name: currency_code
attributes.description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the encumbrance amounts. Typically USD for U.S. water utilities.

attributes.name: encumbrance_description
attributes.description: Detailed narrative description of the purpose and nature of the encumbrance, including goods or services to be acquired.

attributes.name: encumbrance_date
attributes.description: Date the encumbrance was recorded in the financial system, reserving budget funds for the obligation.

attributes.name: encumbrance_number
attributes.description: Business-facing document number for the encumbrance, typically generated by the financial system (SAP or Tyler Munis) for tracking and reference purposes.

attributes.name: encumbrance_status
attributes.description: Current lifecycle status of the encumbrance: open (active and uncommitted balance remains), partially_liquidated (some invoices applied), fully_liquidated (all funds expended), closed (fiscal year-end closure), cancelled (voided before liquidation), or reversed (accounting correction).

attributes.name: encumbrance_type
attributes.description: Classification of the encumbrance stage: pre-encumbrance (requisition stage), encumbrance (purchase order or contract issued), reservation (blanket order), or commitment (other obligating document).

attributes.name: expected_delivery_date
attributes.description: Anticipated date when goods or services covered by the encumbrance are expected to be delivered or completed.

attributes.name: expenditure_category
attributes.description: High-level classification of the encumbrance: capital (CAPEX for infrastructure and equipment), operating (OPEX for day-to-day operations), debt_service (principal and interest payments), or grant (grant-funded expenditure).

attributes.name: fiscal_year
attributes.description: Fiscal year in which the encumbrance was created and against which budget appropriation is reserved (e.g., 2024).

attributes.name: fund_type
attributes.description: Classification of the fund: governmental (general, special revenue, debt service, capital projects, permanent), proprietary (enterprise, internal service), or fiduciary (pension, investment trust, private-purpose trust, custodial).

attributes.name: last_modified_timestamp
attributes.description: Timestamp when the encumbrance record was last updated in the lakehouse silver layer, capturing any changes to status, amounts, or other attributes.

attributes.name: liquidated_amount
attributes.description: Cumulative amount of the encumbrance that has been liquidated (expended) through invoice payments or other expenditure transactions.

attributes.name: notes
attributes.description: Free-text field for additional comments, special instructions, or contextual information related to the encumbrance.

attributes.name: originating_document_date
attributes.description: Date the originating document (purchase order, contract, etc.) was issued or executed, establishing the commitment.

attributes.name: originating_document_number
attributes.description: Document number of the source transaction that created this encumbrance (e.g., PO number, contract number, requisition number).

attributes.name: originating_document_type
attributes.description: Type of source document that created the encumbrance: purchase order, contract, blanket order, requisition, work order, or service agreement.

attributes.name: remaining_balance
attributes.description: Unliquidated balance of the encumbrance, calculated as encumbrance_amount minus liquidated_amount, representing funds still reserved for future expenditure.

attributes.name: requisitioner_name
attributes.description: Name of the employee or department that initiated the requisition or purchase request leading to the encumbrance.

attributes.name: reversal_date
attributes.description: Date the encumbrance was reversed, if applicable.

attributes.name: reversal_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the encumbrance has been reversed due to an accounting correction or cancellation. True if reversed, False otherwise.

attributes.name: reversal_reason
attributes.description: Explanation or reason code for why the encumbrance was reversed (e.g., vendor cancellation, budget reallocation, data entry error).

attributes.name: source_system_code
attributes.description: Unique identifier of the encumbrance record in the source operational system (SAP document number, Tyler Munis encumbrance ID).

attributes.name: year_end_carryforward_flag
attributes.description: Indicates whether the encumbrance is eligible to be carried forward to the next fiscal year if not fully liquidated by year-end. True if carryforward is allowed, False otherwise.

products.name: bank_account
products.description: Treasury management for the water utility's bank accounts and reconciliation activities. Covers account master data (bank name, account number, account type, fund association, authorized signatories, balance limits, sweep arrangements, investment policy compliance) and monthly reconciliation records (GL balance vs. bank statement balance, outstanding checks, deposits in transit, reconciling items, preparer/reviewer/approval). Supports cash management, internal controls, external audit requirements, and GASB cash and investment disclosures.
products.reference: SAP FI Bank Master / Treasury Management

products.name: project_funding_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the funding allocation contract between grant and cip_project. It captures the specific terms, amounts, and compliance requirements for how each grant funds each CIP project. Each record links one grant to one cip_project with attributes that exist only in the context of this funding relationship, including allocation amounts, eligible cost categories, drawdown schedules, and grant-specific compliance requirements.. Existence Justification: In water utility operations, CIP projects are routinely funded by blending multiple funding sources: federal SRF loans, EPA WIFIA loans, state grants, USDA Rural Development grants, and local bonds. A single large infrastructure project (e.g., $50M treatment plant upgrade) may draw from 3-5 different grant programs, each with distinct allocation amounts, eligible cost categories, drawdown schedules, and compliance requirements. Conversely, a single large grant award (e.g., EPA Clean Water SRF) is typically allocated across multiple CIP projects within the utility's capital program. The allocation relationship is actively managed by finance/grants staff who track drawdowns, ensure compliance, and report to grantors on a per-project, per-grant basis.

products.name: grant_allocation
products.description: This association product represents the allocation of grant funding to specific lift station capital improvement projects. It captures the financial relationship between a grant award and the infrastructure assets it funds. Each record links one lift station to one grant with project-specific funding details, expenditure tracking, compliance milestones, and reimbursement status required for grantor reporting and GASB grant accounting.. Existence Justification: Water utilities routinely fund capital improvements to multiple lift stations using a single grant award (e.g., an EPA WIFIA loan for system-wide pump efficiency upgrades, or an ARPA resilience grant covering backup power at 10 stations). Conversely, a single lift station rehabilitation project often requires funding from multiple grant sources (e.g., 50% SRF loan, 25% state energy efficiency grant, 25% local match). The utility must track project-specific expenditures, reimbursement requests, and compliance certifications for each lift station-grant combination to support grantor reporting, GASB accounting, and single audit requirements.

products.name: grant_funded_segment
products.description: This association product represents the funding relationship between sewer network segments and infrastructure grants. It captures the allocation of grant funds to specific sewer rehabilitation or replacement projects, tracking costs, reimbursement status, and compliance with grantor requirements. Each record links one sewer segment to one grant with financial and project phase attributes that exist only in the context of this funding relationship.. Existence Justification: In water utility capital improvement programs, a single sewer segment rehabilitation project is routinely funded by multiple grants simultaneously (e.g., 60% CWSRF, 30% EPA WIFIA, 10% state infrastructure bank), and each grant award covers multiple sewer segments across the service area. Grant administrators actively manage these funding relationships to track cost allocation, ensure compliance with each grantor's allowable cost categories, prepare segment-specific drawdown requests, and report project progress to multiple agencies. This is an operational funding management process, not an analytical correlation.
